title: Fix #13957: don't pass is_class to ForwardRef on interpreters without it
body:
Fixes #13957

On Python 3.10, defining a model with a string (forward-ref) annotation raised:

```
TypeError: ForwardRef.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'is_class'
```

`typing.ForwardRef` only gained the `is_class` parameter on newer interpreters, but `_type_convert()` passed it unconditionally.

`_type_convert()` now falls back to constructing the `ForwardRef` without `is_class` when the interpreter rejects the argument, keeping the intended `is_argument=False` behaviour.

Added a regression test that swaps in a `ForwardRef` without `is_class` support; it fails on the previous revision with the reported `TypeError`.

title: Fix datetime parsing in custom validator examples
body:
## Change Summary

The custom datetime-validator examples inspect `tzinfo` or `utcoffset()` before the datetime handler parses the input. As a result, an ISO datetime string raises `AttributeError`, including when supplied through `TypeAdapter.validate_json()`.

Use the handler's parsed datetime for these checks, and annotate the incoming wrap-validator value as `Any`. Add executable examples for a naive datetime string and an offset-aware JSON string. Existing timezone constraints still apply.

This only changes `docs/examples/custom_validators.md`.

## Related issue number

title: feat: support attribute docstrings inheritance for TypedDict and dataclasses
body:
## Change Summary

When `use_attribute_docstrings=True` is enabled, attribute docstrings declared on base classes were previously dropped for `TypedDict` subclasses and dataclasses because docstring extraction only inspected the leaf class rather than traversing the class hierarchy.

This PR adds inheritance support for attribute docstrings:
1. In `_update_fields_from_docstrings` (`pydantic/_internal/_fields.py`), traverse `reversed(cls.__mro__)` so dataclasses inherit attribute docstrings from base classes while allowing subclasses to override them.
2. In `_generate_schema.py`, traverse `reversed(mro(typed_dict_cls))` (using Pydantic's virtual MRO for `TypedDict`) so inherited `TypedDict` fields retain docstrings from parent `TypedDict`s and can override them.
3. Remove the `@pytest.mark.xfail` marker from `test_stdlib_docs_extraction_inheritance()` in `tests/test_docs_extraction.py`.
4. Add comprehensive unit tests covering Pydantic dataclass inheritance, `TypedDict` inheritance, and `TypedDict` docstring overrides.
5. Update documentation warning in `pydantic/config.py` to reflect that inheritance is now supported for `TypedDict` and dataclasses.

## Related issue number

References #13468. Addresses the inheritance limitation tracked by the `test_stdlib_docs_extraction_inheritance` xfail test.

## Validation

- `pytest tests/test_docs_extraction.py`: 19 passed (was 15 passed, 1 xfailed).
- `pytest tests/test_fields.py`: 71 passed.
- `pytest tests/test_dataclasses.py`: 269 passed, 3 skipped, 1 xfailed (unrelated).
- `pytest tests/test_json_schema.py`: 659 passed, 5 skipped, 2 xfailed.

body:
I was skeptical if this was a good idea (at first, it felt weird to have potential errors related to failed resolution of forward references raised during serialization), but we already do this during validation anyway, and the potential error raised is strictly better that the confusing `TypeError: 'MockValSer' object cannot be converted to 'SchemaSerializer'` one we have today.

We don't provide any namespace depth on purpose, to avoid resolving types from unrelated places, so if it succeeds it should be guaranteed to resolve types properly.

title: fix: route named __pydantic_init_subclass__ kwargs away from object.__init_subclass__
body:
Fixes #13300

## Problem

When a subclass defines `__pydantic_init_subclass__` with explicit named parameters and those names are passed as class keywords, `object.__init_subclass__()` raises `TypeError: object.__init_subclass__() takes no keyword arguments`.

```python
class Event(BaseModel):
    @classmethod
    def __pydantic_init_subclass__(cls, event_type: str | None = None, **kwargs):
        super().__pydantic_init_subclass__(**kwargs)

class CreatedEvent(Event, event_type='created'):  # TypeError
    pass
```

## Root Cause

`ConfigWrapper.for_model()` strips known pydantic config keys from `kwargs` in-place, but any remaining kwargs (e.g. `event_type='created'`) are passed directly to `super().__new__()` at line 133, which triggers Python's `__init_subclass__` chain. Since `BaseModel` has no runtime `__init_subclass__`, the unknown kwargs reach `object.__init_subclass__()` → `TypeError`.

`__pydantic_init_subclass__` is called later at line 267, but never gets a chance because the crash happens first.

## Fix

Before calling `super().__new__()`, inspect the MRO for a `__pydantic_init_subclass__` that declares named parameters. Extract those named kwargs from `kwargs` (leaving `**kwargs`-only handlers untouched) and pass them to `__pydantic_init_subclass__` instead.

This preserves all existing behavior:
- Classes passing unknown kwargs still raise `TypeError` (no named params to extract)
- Classes with only `**kwargs` in `__pydantic_init_subclass__` are unaffected
- The existing `test_pydantic_hooks` test passes unchanged

title: Skip the generic pickle test when cloudpickle is absent
body:
## Change Summary

`test_generic_model_pickle_different_module` fails with `IndexError: list index out of range` in an environment that does not have `cloudpickle` installed.

The test spawns a subprocess whose code does `import cloudpickle`. `cloudpickle` is declared in the `testing-extra` dependency group rather than `dev` ([pyproject.toml](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/pyproject.toml)), so it is absent from a default environment. The child then dies before printing anything, and the parent fails at `creator.stdout.splitlines()[0]` on an empty stdout, an error that gives no indication of its cause.

This skips the test when `cloudpickle` is unavailable, using the same guard [tests/test_pickle.py](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/main/tests/test_pickle.py) already uses for this exact dependency: the import is skipped outright on PyPy, and otherwise guarded with `try`/`except ImportError`. Both halves matter. `importlib.util.find_spec` was the shorter alternative and was avoided deliberately, because it reports a package that is on disk yet fails to import as present. And PyPy has to be excluded up front rather than caught, because there `import cloudpickle` raises `AttributeError` rather than `ImportError`, so a `try`/`except ImportError` does not contain it, and since the import happens at module level during collection, the failure surfaces as a collection error for the whole file before any `skipif` is consulted.

It also asserts the subprocess return code, so a failure from any other cause (a pydantic / pydantic-core version skew between parent and child, a syntax error in the generated code, or a timeout) reports itself instead of surfacing as the same opaque `IndexError`.

### A note on the PyPy failure this initially introduced

The first version of this PR guarded the import with `try`/`except ImportError` only, and passed every check available on CPython. CI caught that it is not enough: on PyPy, `import cloudpickle` raises `AttributeError: type object 'Pickler' has no attribute 'dispatch'`, which that guard does not catch, and because the import is at module level the failure became a collection error for the whole file. The guard now mirrors `test_pickle.py` in full, and the PyPy path is therefore the one that file already exercises.

### Verification

The failure reproduces on a checkout without `testing-extra`, and was confirmed to come from the child's import by capturing its stderr:

```text
subprocess returncode : 1
subprocess stderr     : ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'cloudpickle'
subprocess stdout     : ''          # so .splitlines()[0] raises IndexError
```

Results for `pytest tests/ --ignore=tests/pydantic_core --ignore=tests/mypy`:

| environment | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| without `cloudpickle` | `1 failed, 6184 passed` | `6184 passed, 28 xfailed` |
| with `cloudpickle` | `6207 passed` | `6207 passed, 28 xfailed` |

`tests/test_generics.py` specifically: `122 passed, 4 xfailed` without it (only this test skips, the rest of the module still runs), `123 passed, 4 xfailed` with it.

`ruff check .` and `ruff format --check` are clean. The change is confined to `tests/test_generics.py`; no production code is touched.

## Related issue number

None. This corrects a test-harness failure rather than a defect in `pydantic`, and `CONTRIBUTING.md` asks for an issue first unless the change is trivial. This is a 13-line, test-only guard with no behaviour change, so I read it as falling under that exemption. Happy to open an issue if that is the wrong call.

title: Explicitly enable frame pointers
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! -->
<!-- Unless your change is trivial, please create an issue to discuss the change before creating a PR -->

## Change Summary

[PEP 831](https://peps.python.org/pep-0831/) ([What's New in 3.15](https://docs.python.org/3.15/whatsnew/3.15.html#whatsnew315-frame-pointers)): starting with Python 3.15, CPython is built by default with [`-fno-omit-frame-pointer`](https://clang.llvm.org/docs/ClangCommandLineReference.html#cmdoption-clang-fomit-frame-pointer) and [`-mno-omit-leaf-frame-pointer`](https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/gcc/x86-Options.html#index-mno-omit-leaf-frame-pointer-3), i.e. frame pointers are kept in every function, including leaf functions (functions that don't call anything else).

These flags are exposed through [`sysconfig`](https://docs.python.org/3.15/library/sysconfig.html#sysconfig.get_config_var), so C extensions built by tools that read Python's build configuration (e.g. setuptools) inherit them automatically. For everything else, the What's New entry says:

> Build systems that compile C, C++, Rust, or other native code without inheriting Python's compiler flags should enable equivalent frame-pointer flags themselves. A single native component built without frame pointers can break stack unwinding for the whole Python process.

### Where Rust / PyO3 / maturin stand

- `rustc` doesn't read `sysconfig` flags. maturin, PyO3's build scripts and maturin-action don't add frame-pointer flags either. Until now, pydantic-core got rustc's per-target default.
- That default is controlled by [`-C force-frame-pointers`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/rustc/codegen-options/index.html#force-frame-pointers) and depends on the target. As of rustc 1.97.1:

  | Target | Default | Why |
  |---|---|---|
  | [`aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu`](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/1.97.1/compiler/rustc_target/src/spec/targets/aarch64_unknown_linux_gnu.rs#L22) | kept in non-leaf functions | [rust-lang/rust#140832](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/140832): the [AArch64 procedure call standard](https://github.com/ARM-software/abi-aa/blob/4492d1570eb70c8fd146623e0db65b2d241f12e7/aapcs64/aapcs64.rst#the-frame-pointer) lets each platform define frame-pointer requirements. [Apple](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/xcode/writing-arm64-code-for-apple-platforms) and [Windows](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/cpp/build/arm64-windows-abi-conventions?view=msvc-170) mandate them; for Linux, Rust follows clang (non-leaf). |
  | Apple [`x86_64` / `aarch64`](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/1.97.1/compiler/rustc_target/src/spec/base/apple/mod.rs#L153-L159) | always / non-leaf | Follows Apple platform conventions. |
  | [`x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/1.97.1/compiler/rustc_target/src/spec/targets/x86_64_unknown_linux_gnu.rs) | **may omit** | No override, so it uses the [global default](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/1.97.1/compiler/rustc_target/src/spec/mod.rs#L2854). Enabling non-leaf frame pointers everywhere was benchmarked in [rust-lang/rust#115521](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/115521) and judged "a pretty hard sell" performance-wise; it's still unmerged. |

- The prebuilt Rust standard library shipped by [rustup](https://rust-lang.github.io/rustup/) *is* built with `-Cforce-frame-pointers=non-leaf` ([`[profile.dist]` in `library/Cargo.toml`](https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/1.97.1/library/Cargo.toml#L60-L73)), so std frames don't break the chain. Only our own code does.

**Net effect before this PR:** on x86_64 Linux (the most common deployment target), a profiler walking the stack of a 3.15 process loses the chain as soon as it enters `_pydantic_core`. On aarch64 Linux and macOS it mostly works already (except in leaf functions).

### This PR

Adds `-C force-frame-pointers=yes` to `pydantic-core/.cargo/config.toml` for all targets except wasm ([Pyodide](https://pyodide.org/) builds, where native profilers don't apply):

- It is a [`target.'cfg(...)'`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#targetcfgrustflags) entry rather than [`build.rustflags`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#buildrustflags), because Cargo ignores `build.rustflags` as soon as any `target.*` entry matches, and our existing macOS [`target.<triple>`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#targettriplerustflags) entries would silently disable it. Matching `target.<triple>` and `target.<cfg>` entries are joined together. The wasm exclusion uses [`target_family`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/conditional-compilation.html#r-cfg.target_family).
- `yes` rather than `non-leaf`: `non-leaf` requires `-Zunstable-options`, which only works on nightly. `yes` also matches CPython, which keeps frame pointers in leaf functions too.
- Checked locally (aarch64 macOS): `maturin build -v` passes the flag alongside the macOS link args, and maturin's PGO flags are [appended to the configured rustflags](https://github.com/PyO3/maturin/blob/4c4d695109ef2799d6331681f9cafbccc4722bac/src/compile.rs#L427-L446) rather than replacing them. As with any config rustflags, setting `RUSTFLAGS` (e.g. `make build-coverage`) overrides them.

### Performance

The only target where this meaningfully changes codegen is x86_64 Linux, which is also where Rust decided the cost wasn't worth making it the default. CodSpeed runs on x86_64 Linux, so its results on this PR show the actual cost for pydantic-core.

title: Don't leak AliasPath keys into model_extra in model_construct
body:
## Change Summary

`model_construct` pops field names and `str` validation aliases out of the input dict before assigning the leftovers to `__pydantic_extra__`, but the `AliasPath` branch only read via `search_dict_for_path` without removing anything. With `extra='allow'`, the alias path's root key leaked into `model_extra` (and could shadow the field's own value in `model_dump`).

The fix records each consumed `AliasPath` root during the field loop and removes those keys from `values` after all fields have been processed, before `_extra` is assigned. Deferring the removal (rather than popping inline) keeps fields that share a path root working, matching `model_validate` behavior. The caller's input is never mutated (`values` is a fresh kwargs dict).

title: Fix non-init fields with validate_assignment=True on Pydantic dataclasses
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! -->
<!-- Unless your change is trivial, please create an issue to discuss the change before creating a PR -->
## Change Summary

Support non-init fields without defaults in Pydantic dataclasses when `validate_assignment=True`.

Previously, dataclass fields with `init=False` and no default value or default factory were skipped during field collection in `collect_dataclass_fields`. As a result, `__pydantic_fields__` did not contain them. When `validate_assignment=True` was configured, setting such fields (for instance, inside `__post_init__`) triggered `__pydantic_validator__.validate_assignment`, raising an `AttributeError: 'X' object has no attribute 'x'` because the attribute was not yet set on the instance.

This PR addresses the issue by:
1. Collecting `init=False` dataclass fields in `collect_dataclass_fields` so they are properly registered in `__pydantic_fields__`.
2. Updating dataclass schema generation field sorting in `_generate_schema.py` to ensure `init=False` fields are sorted after `init=True` positional fields, preserving the expected `__init__` signature.
3. Catching `AttributeError` during assignment validation in `validated_setattr` and setting the attribute via `object.__setattr__` if the field exists in `__pydantic_fields__`.

title: fix: inherit TypedDict closed/extra_items from parent classes (PEP 728)
body:
## Summary

Fixes #13919.

PEP 728 `closed`/`extra_items` support was added in #12179, but three cases from the spec don't work:

1. **`extra_items` not inherited** — A subclass of a TypedDict with `extra_items=int` should also accept extra int items. Pydantic treats the subclass as a plain TypedDict and silently drops the extra keys.

2. **`closed=True` not inherited** — A subclass of a closed TypedDict should also reject extra keys. Pydantic accepts them and drops them instead of raising `extra_forbidden`.

3. **`extra_items=Never` and `extra_items=ReadOnly[int]` fail** — These raise `PydanticSchemaGenerationError`. Per PEP 728, `extra_items=Never` is the same as `closed=True`, and `extra_items` can be wrapped in `ReadOnly[]`.

## Root Cause

In `pydantic/_internal/_generate_schema.py`, `__closed__` and `__extra_items__` are read directly from the class. Per PEP 728, those attributes only reflect what was passed to that exact class, not its parents. TypedDict parents are in `__orig_bases__`, not `__mro__`.

## Fix

In `pydantic/_internal/_generate_schema.py`:
- Walk `__orig_bases__` to find inherited `__closed__` and `__extra_items__` values from parent TypedDicts
- Handle `extra_items=Never` as equivalent to `closed=True`
- Unwrap `ReadOnly[]` from `extra_items` before passing to `generate_schema`

## Changes

- `pydantic/_internal/_generate_schema.py`: Inheritance walk + `Never`/`ReadOnly` handling
- `tests/test_types_typeddict.py`: 4 new regression tests

## Verification

- 4 new tests: RED before fix, GREEN after fix
- All 84 TypedDict tests pass
- Full `test_types.py`: 280 passed, 4 skipped, 1 xfailed
- `ruff check pydantic/_internal/_generate_schema.py`: All checks passed

title: Share structurally identical `nullable` and `default` nodes within a schema build
body:
`Optional[str] = None` — the most common field shape in large model-heavy codebases — builds three validator nodes: `default`, `nullable` and `str`. Leaf validators like `str` are already shared statics, but the two wrapper nodes were built fresh for every field, each one also allocating a `String` for its name. The same applies on the serializer side.

A `nullable` node is fully described by the validator it wraps, and a `default` node by that plus its default value and a few flags, so nodes agreeing on those are interchangeable. This caches them on `DefinitionsBuilder`, keyed by the address of the inner validator (and of the default object).

**Why the addresses are safe as keys:** the cached node holds a strong reference to everything its key names, so an address can't be reused while it is in the cache, and the addresses are only ever compared, never dereferenced. The cache lives on the builder and is dropped when the build finishes — there is no global state, no locking, and nothing outlives the schema being built.

### Measurements

An application defining 2000 models with 20 `Optional[str] = None` fields each:

| | RSS |
| --- | --- |
| before | 121.2MB |
| validators shared | 107.2MB |
| validators + serializers shared | **95.5MB (−21.2%)** |

On `google-genai` (766 models) there's no measurable change — its per-model field shapes vary enough that there's little to share within any one build, and its models are already deduplicated by prebuilt reuse. The win is specific to codebases where the same simple field shapes recur across many models.

Measured on top of #13522 and #13523, so the numbers aren't inflated by the duplicate-tree bug those fix.

Changelog

Sourced from regex's changelog.

1.13.1 (2026-07-15)

This is a release that fixes a bug where incorrect regex match offsets could be reported. Note that this doesn't impact whether a match occurs or not, just where it occurs. The match offsets are still valid for slicing, they just may not refer to the correct leftmost-first match. See #1364 for (many) more details.

Bug fixes:

  • #1354: Fixes previously unsound reverse suffix and inner optimizations.

1.13.0 (2026-07-09)

This release includes a new API, a regex! macro, for lazy compilation of a regex from a string literal. If you use regexes a lot, it's likely you've already written one exactly like it. The new macro can be used like this:

use regex::regex;

fn is_match(line: &str) -> bool {

// The regex will be compiled approximately once and reused automatically.

// This avoids the footgun of using Regex::new here, which would

// guarantee that it would be compiled every time this routine is called.

// This would likely make this routine much slower than it needs to be.

regex!(r"bar|baz").is_match(line)

}


let hay = "

path/to/foo:54:Blue Harvest

path/to/bar:90:Something, Something, Something, Dark Side

path/to/baz:3:It's a Trap!

";


let matches = hay.lines().filter(|line| is_match(line)).count();

assert_eq!(matches, 2);

Improvements:

  • #709: Add a new regex! macro for efficient and automatic reuse of a compiled regex.

title: Handle OS errors during `ZoneInfo` validation
body: Fixes #13908. Validating a ZoneInfo field with a tzdata directory name ('America', 'Etc') or an over-long key raises a raw OSError subclass instead of ValidationError, so a user-supplied timezone can crash e.g. a web API with an unhandled exception. Root cause: validate_str_is_valid_iana_tz only catches (ZoneInfoNotFoundError, ValueError, TypeError), but ZoneInfo() hits the filesystem and raises OSError subclasses for these inputs (IsADirectoryError on POSIX / PermissionError on Windows for directory names on Python < 3.13 per CPython gh-85702; ENAMETOOLONG / EINVAL for over-long keys - I reproduced both cases, including the Windows PermissionError variant). Fix: catch OSError alongside the existing exceptions so all invalid keys surface as zoneinfo_str errors. Single call site, no behavior change for valid zones. Tests: new parametrized test_zoneinfo_parsing_fails_for_os_errors in tests/test_types_zoneinfo.py asserting the full error shape for both cases. Verified: all 9 tests in the file pass on Python 3.11 with tzdata installed; ruff check and format clean. (The one test_datetime.py timedelta failure also fails on pristine main in this env - pre-existing, unrelated.)

body:
Bumps [urllib3](https://github.com/urllib3/urllib3) from 2.7.0 to 2.8.0.
Release notes

Sourced from urllib3's releases.

2.8.0

🚀 urllib3 is fundraising for HTTP/2 support

urllib3 is raising ~$40,000 USD to release HTTP/2 support and ensure long-term sustainable maintenance of the project. If your company or organization uses Python and would benefit from HTTP/2 support in Requests, pip, cloud SDKs, and thousands of other projects please consider contributing financially to ensure HTTP/2 support is developed sustainably and maintained for the long-haul.

Thank you for your support.

Security

Fixed the following security issues:

  • The TLS configuration for HTTPS proxies could be ignored or overridden. (High severity, GHSA-8988-9cw3-xx77)
  • HTTPResponse.stream() and read_chunked() could buffer a chunk-size line of unbounded length in memory. (High severity, GHSA-vxq7-64xx-v4gw)
  • Chunked Deflate streaming could enter an infinite loop. (Medium severity, GHSA-gh4c-6fx4-qh6g)

[!IMPORTANT] urllib3 2.8.0 fixes HTTPS proxy TLS configuration being ignored or overridden by destination settings. Configurations relying on that behavior may require changes.

Configure proxy CA certificates and client certificates in proxy_ssl_context, and proxy identity checks with proxy_assert_hostname or proxy_assert_fingerprint. Destination client certificates and identity overrides no longer apply to HTTPS forwarding proxy connections.

[!NOTE] CVE IDs had not yet been assigned to these advisories at the time of release due to a backlog at GitHub's CNA.

Deprecations & Removals

  • Deprecated using an empty collection as the Retry option allowed_methods to retry any verb. (#5044)

Features

  • Added Url.auth_decoded and Url.auth_decoded_joined convenience properties to the result of parse_url(). (#4945)
  • Added basic_auth_encoding and proxy_basic_auth_encoding parameters to urllib3.util.make_headers(). (#5092)

Bugfixes

  • Fixed response header handling to replace obsolete folded header lines (obs-fold) with spaces in accordance with RFC 9112, preventing raw CRLF sequences from appearing in header values such as Set-Cookie. (#1362)

  • Fixed usage of proxy_ssl_context with ProxyManager when use_forwarding_for_https=True. Passing ssl_context instead of proxy_ssl_context for HTTPS proxies in this configuration now emits a FutureWarning and will raise an error in v3.0. (#2577)

  • Changed behavior of the default ConnectionPool.pool initialization. LifoQueue is now resolved from the queue module after the ConnectionPool is instantiated instead of using the default cached QueueCls class property. This is done because sometimes the queue.LifoQueue is monkey-patched late in the program, such as by gevent. (#3289)

  • Raised UnrewindableBodyError instead of ValueError when retrying a request whose body had tell() but not seek(). (#3779)

  • Decoded percent-encoded SOCKS proxy credentials before authenticating with the proxy server. (#3785)

  • Fixed HTTPResponse.drain_conn() to discard unread response data in 64 KiB chunks (same as the default amt when doing HTTPResponse.stream(...)). (#5019)

  • Fixed is_ipaddress() to detect non-standard IPv4 forms accepted by socket.connect, such as hex (0x7f000001), octal (0177.0.0.1), and decimal integers (2130706433), ensuring SSL certificate verification uses the correct mode for these addresses. (#5029)

  • Fixed HTTPConnectionPool.urlopen raising a misleading FullPoolError instead of ValueError when called with an invalid timeout argument on a pool created with block=True. (#5059)

  • Fixed port-zero handling to preserve explicit :0 values instead of substituting the default ports 80 or 443 in URL parsing, pool selection, proxy configuration, connection_from_url(), and HTTP/2 request authority. (#5071, #5101)

  • Fixed a bug where PoolManager passed the assert_hostname and assert_fingerprint parameters to HTTP connection pools. (#5077)

  • Fixed HTTPConnectionPool.urlopen() and HTTP proxy forwarding to strip URL fragments from absolute request targets before sending requests. (#5079)

  • Added safeguards to the proxy tunneling code to prevent potential security issues when handling invalid characters in the proxy host and HTTP headers. This change affects users of Python 3.10, Python 3.11, and Python 3.12 when the standard library does not contain the fix; those on newer Python versions should upgrade to 3.13.14+ or 3.14.5+ to get the same security fixes. (#5091)

  • Fixed HTTPSConnection.connect() overriding ProxyConfig.ssl_context's certificate policy and proxy identity checks with the target connection's TLS settings when forwarding through an HTTPS proxy.

    HTTPSConnection no longer applies target SNI, assertions, or client credentials to forwarding proxy handshakes and continues to use its ssl_context as a fallback when an HTTPS proxy forwards an HTTP target. (#5093)

  • Fixed URL parsing to more strictly enforce RFC 3986 host syntax, rejecting invalid host input such as raw spaces and control characters, malformed percent-encodings, and percent-encoded control characters in HTTP(S) hosts and IPv6 zone identifiers, including proxy CONNECT tunnel targets. Host normalization now also follows RFC 3986 normalization rules for percent-encoded octets by decoding percent-encoded unreserved characters and uppercasing the hexadecimal digits of retained percent-encoded octets. (#5095)

title: Fix docs example that cannot raise the `PydanticUndefinedAnnotation` it documents
body:
## Change Summary

One-word change to the footnote example in `docs/internals/resolving_annotations.md`, so that it raises the error it documents.

The footnote exists to show that a function's locals are held by weak reference and may not resolve during a later `model_rebuild()`. Its example binds `A = int`. But `int` is a static type that lives for the whole process, so the weak reference never goes stale: the rebuild succeeds, `f` resolves to `int | str`, and the comment on the last line (`PydanticUndefinedAnnotation: name 'A' is not defined`) never happens. A reader who copies the snippet sees the opposite of what the paragraph above it says.

Binding `A = list[int]` instead makes the example raise exactly the documented error. The alias is created inside `func()`, nothing else references it, so it is dropped by refcounting when `func()` returns and the weak reference is dead by the time `model_rebuild()` runs.

I tried the obvious fix first, a local `class A`, and it is not enough. A class only dies under the cyclic collector, so without an explicit `gc.collect()` it is still alive at rebuild time, the name resolves, and the rebuild fails with `PydanticSchemaGenerationError` for the plain class rather than with the undefined-annotation error. That would make the example fail for the wrong reason and turn the comment into a different lie. Candidates I ran, each in a fresh process with no `gc.collect()`, on `main` at 2.14.0b2 / pydantic_core 2.49.0:

| local binding | result of `model_rebuild(_types_namespace={'Forward': str})` |
| --- | --- |
| `A = int` (current docs) | no exception, `f` resolves to `int \| str` |
| `class A: pass` | `PydanticSchemaGenerationError` (class still alive, wrong error) |
| `class A(BaseModel): pass` | no exception, resolves to `A \| str` (class still alive) |
| `A = int \| None` | no exception |
| `A = Annotated[int, 'x']` | no exception |
| `A = list[int]` | `PydanticUndefinedAnnotation: name 'A' is not defined` |
| `A = NewType('A', int)` | `PydanticUndefinedAnnotation: name 'A' is not defined` |

title: Fix config propagation of stdlib dataclasses and `TypedDict`s in JSON Schema
body:
## Summary

Stdlib dataclasses and `TypedDict`s without their own config inherit the parent config (see [configuration propagation](https://pydantic.dev/docs/validation/latest/concepts/config/#configuration-propagation)). Core schema generation already does this, but JSON Schema generation pushed an empty config (`{}`) for these types instead of `None`, so they didn't inherit it. As a result, the JSON Schema didn't match validation or serialization behavior.

The parent config is now inherited when generating the JSON Schema of these types. If the type has its own config, it is still used. Class-level JSON Schema settings (`title`, `json_schema_extra`, etc.) from the parent are still not applied.

## Examples

Validation:

```python
from dataclasses import dataclass

from typing_extensions import TypedDict

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict


@dataclass
class DC:
    name: str


class TD(TypedDict):
    name: str


class Model(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(str_max_length=5)

    dc: DC
    td: TD


Model(dc={'name': 'too long'}, td={'name': 'too long'})
#> ValidationError: 2 validation errors (for `dc.name` and `td.name`)

print(Model.model_json_schema()['$defs']['DC']['properties']['name'])
# Before: {'title': 'Name', 'type': 'string'}
# After:  {'maxLength': 5, 'title': 'Name', 'type': 'string'}
# (Same for `TD`)

title: fix: reflect Field(init=False) in dataclass metadata
body:
## Change

`as_dataclass_field()` converts a Pydantic `FieldInfo` into a stdlib `dataclasses.field()`, but it dropped the `init` argument — so a field declared with `Field(init=False)` still carried `init=True` in the dataclass metadata.

That had three observable consequences (reproduced on 2.13.5 and `main`):

- the excluded field appeared in `__init__` and `__match_args__`, so positional pattern matching bound the wrong value;
- `dataclasses.replace()` fed the field back into the constructor and raised `unexpected_keyword_argument` under `extra='forbid'`;
- replacing `Field` with `dataclasses.field` in the same example worked, confirming the drop was in the Pydantic-to-stdlib conversion.

This propagates `pydantic_field.init` when set, mirroring how `kw_only` and `repr` are already handled. The `init` default (`None` → stdlib `True`) is untouched, so fields without an explicit `init` behave exactly as before.

## Regression test

`test_init_false_reflected_in_dataclass_metadata` in `tests/test_dataclasses.py`, parametrized over both `pydantic.Field` and `dataclasses.field`, asserts:

- `dataclasses.fields()` reports `init=False` for the excluded field and `True` for the rest;
- `__match_args__` excludes it;
- `dataclasses.replace()` succeeds without feeding the field back into `__init__`.

## Validation

- `uv run pytest tests/test_dataclasses.py -q` → 268 passed, 2 skipped, 1 xfailed.
- `uv run ruff check pydantic/_internal/_dataclasses.py tests/test_dataclasses.py` → clean.

Fixes #13833.

title: fix: stdlib dataclass JSON schema inherits parent model's extra config
body:
`dataclass_schema()` used `getattr(cls, '__pydantic_config__', {})` — an empty-dict fallback — which caused `_config_wrapper_stack.push({})` to silently replace the enclosing model's config with an empty one. `generate_inner()` would then see no `extra='forbid'` and skip emitting `additionalProperties: false`, even when the parent `BaseModel` had `extra='forbid'`.

**Reproduction:**
```python
import dataclasses
from pydantic import BaseModel
from pydantic.config import ConfigDict

@dataclasses.dataclass
class Inner:
    x: int

class Outer(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra='forbid')
    inner: Inner

schema = Outer.model_json_schema()
# Before fix: Inner schema has no `additionalProperties: false`
# After fix:  Inner schema correctly includes `additionalProperties: false`
```

**Fix:** pass `None` when the class has no `__pydantic_config__` so that `push(None)` is a no-op and the parent config is preserved. Then derive `config` for `_update_class_schema` from the effective stack tail when `own_config` is absent.

The validation path in `_generate_schema.py` already applies this pattern (PR #10928). This PR applies the same fix to the JSON-schema path.

Fixes #13845

title: Fix #13817: remove double-visitation of validator tree in ValidatorCallable and ValidatorIterator
body:
Hey, this fixes the GC crash reported in #13817.

Long story short: when you use a `mode='wrap'` field validator and the handler outlives the validation call (which happens when a ValidationError keeps it alive in its traceback), Python's GC ends up traversing the validator tree twice. Once through the parent validator's `impl_py_gc_traverse!`, and once through `ValidatorCallable.__traverse__`. Both traverse the same `Arc<CombinedValidator>`, so refcounts get incremented twice. That corrupts things enough to crash — SIGSEGV in release builds, abort in debug builds.

I saw this personally: debug build abort after a few iterations, release build segfault. The reporter said django-ninja hits this on every failed request.

The fix is straightforward — remove the redundant traversal:

- `ValidatorCallable` (function.rs): dropped `__traverse__` entirely. The parent `FunctionWrapValidator` already traverses the validator tree, so `ValidatorCallable` doesn't need to.
- `ValidatorIterator` (generator.rs): removed the `self.validator.py_gc_traverse()` call but kept `self.iterator.py_gc_traverse()`. The iterator traversal is needed for GC correctness (it holds Py references), but the validator traversal was the duplicate one.

I tested by running 500 iterations of wrap-validator validation with forced errors in a Python debug build — no abort. Also ran the existing wrap validator tests, they pass. The custom test I wrote exercises the exact scenario from the bug report.

title: Harden the pure-annotation schema caches: a key collision, a retention bound, and a checking mode
body:
## Change Summary

Three additions to #13544, stacked so they can be merged into it directly. One is a correctness fix, one answers the open review comment on #13542, and one is the evidence for both. Targeting `field-fast-path` because the changes span both PRs' code.

### 1. `Tuple` and `Tuple[()]` must not share a cache entry

Both have `tuple` as their origin and an empty `get_args()`, so `pure_annotation_cache_key()` returns `(tuple,)` for each — but bare `Tuple` is a variadic tuple of anything and `Tuple[()]` is the empty tuple, and their schemas differ by `variadic_item_index`. Whichever is built first decides what the other one validates.

`tests/test_edge_cases.py::test_pep585_generic_types` **fails on `field-fast-path` when run on its own** (both parametrizations); the full suite happens to build the two forms in the order that hides it. Confirmed to be the caches: forcing them to decline makes it pass.

The two are told apart by whether the alias carries `__args__` at all.

### 2. Bound what a cache key retains, not just how many there are

`CACHE_SIZE_LIMIT` caps the number of entries, but a key can hold a `str`, `bytes` or `int` of any size and is retained until the cache is reset. The reviewer comment on #13542 reported this for `Literal` values; measuring found **three more paths** with the same behaviour:

| path | 8 models × a distinct 1 MB value | after |
|---|---|---|
| `Literal` values | 8.00 MB retained | 0 |
| `str`/`bytes` defaults | 8.00 MB | 0 |
| strings inside encoded metadata | 8.00 MB | 0 |
| `alias`/`title`/`description` in the field-schema key | 8.00 MB | 0 |

The last one matters most in practice — every OpenAPI-documented field has a description, and it goes into the key as it is. `int` is included because python integers are unbounded (`10 ** 1_000_000` as a default is over 400 KB).

A value that large is unique to its field, so its entry would never have been reused; refusing it costs nothing. Measured on the shapes in #13545, the extra length check is within noise.

### 3. A checking mode, and the edge cases it exposed

`PYDANTIC_VERIFY_SCHEMA_CACHE=1` builds every field schema a second time with the caches emptied and compares the two structurally, reporting totals at the end of the run:

```
schema caches: 21,923 field schemas checked against an uncached build, 0 differed
```

It lives in the test suite, not in `pydantic/`, so it costs the shipped diff nothing — emptying the cache dicts in place is enough to force the long way round. **This is what found the `Tuple` collision above.**

Plus 110 edge-case tests, each checked by removing the guard it covers and confirming it goes red:

- **99 combinations of config setting × pure annotation**, comparing generated schemas with the cache cleared in between. The "no configuration can affect a pure annotation's schema" claim currently holds for all of them; this is what fails if a future setting breaks it. (Worth noting for anyone writing more: `str_strip_whitespace` is invisible here because it goes through the model's core config, and an enum under `use_enum_values` carries a `ref` — `arbitrary_types_allowed` is one that does reach a schema.)
- a hook monkeypatched onto a trusted leaf class **after** it has been cached, and an in-place mutation of `AnyUrl._constraints` — both already handled correctly, neither previously pinned down
- one `Field()` reused by two models, equal mutable defaults not being shared, `Literal` over an enum member not treated as pure

## Validation

- `12,470 passed`, plus one pre-existing environment failure (`test_exports.py::test_public_internal`, a mypy plugin version clash)
- checking mode: 21,923 field schemas, 0 differed
- **free-threaded 3.14t**: all 169 cache tests pass; a 16-thread × 250-model stress test (4,000 models, caches hitting their size limit so the clear-then-assign path runs under contention) reports zero problems over three runs. Shown non-vacuous: collapsing `Literal` keys makes one thread receive another's schema.
- `ruff check` and `ruff format` clean

## A note on the numbers

Measured against the merge-base as a separate checkout (not by disabling the caches from inside the branch, which flatters them — a disabled-but-still-storing baseline pays for work it never uses):

| | main | branch | |
|---|---|---|---|
| 600 models × 3 `Optional[str]` | 447 ms | 319 ms | −28.8% |
| mixed field shapes | 505 ms | 391 ms | −22.6% |
| `Annotated[str, Field(max_length=10)]` | 659 ms | 517 ms | −21.6% |
| `import mcp` (50 pairs) | 1226 ms | 1200 ms | +2.1% |
| `import fastmcp` (50 pairs) | 596 ms | 595 ms | nothing |

Consistent with the caveat in #13545: the win is on per-model class-definition time, and whole-library imports dilute it. `import fastmcp` is only ~37% model definition.

## Known gaps

- `typing.Any` is in `_PURE_LEAF_TYPES` and, since 3.11, is a mutable python class — `Any.__get_pydantic_core_schema__ = ...` sticks, so "immutable C types only" is not quite true and a hook on `Any` would be reachable. Obscure, and closing it costs a lookup on the hottest path or moving `Any` into the verified-leaf map; left alone deliberately.
- Three existing tests count `__get_pydantic_core_schema__` invocations and so fail under the checking mode, which builds twice. They are deselected when running it rather than modified:
  `tests/test_annotated.py::test_modify_get_schema_annotated`,
  `tests/test_internal.py::test_trusted_leaf_class_rejects_monkeypatched_hook`,
  `tests/test_main.py::test_get_core_schema_unpacks_refs_for_source_type`.

title: Fix #13817: remove double-visitation of validator tree in ValidatorCallable and ValidatorIterator
body:
## Summary

- Fixes #13817 by removing `__traverse__` from `ValidatorCallable` and removing the validator traversal from `ValidatorIterator.__traverse__`
- Prevents double-visitation of the `Arc<CombinedValidator>` tree which corrupted refcounts and caused crashes (SIGSEGV in release, abort in debug builds)

## Root Cause

When a `ValidatorCallable` or `ValidatorIterator` is kept alive (e.g. in a traceback after a `ValidationError`), Python's GC traverses both the parent validator (which traverses the `Arc<CombinedValidator>` via `impl_py_gc_traverse!`) and the child wrapper (which traverses the same `Arc<CombinedValidator>` via its own `__traverse__`). This double-visitation increments refcounts twice, corrupting them and leading to crashes.

## Changes

- **`ValidatorCallable`** (function.rs): Removed `__traverse__` entirely
- **`ValidatorIterator`** (generator.rs): Removed `self.validator.py_gc_traverse()` call, kept `self.iterator.py_gc_traverse()` which is needed for GC correctness

## Testing

- Custom test: 500 iterations of mode='wrap' validation with forced errors — no crash
- Existing wrap validator tests: pass
- Python debug build: no abort

body:
## Change Summary

In `pydantic._internal._fields.resolve_default_value`, `smart_deepcopy` was imported inside the function body on every invocation:

title: Fix dead isinstance check in `_decorator_infos_for_class()`
body:
## What

`_decorator_infos_for_class`'s final `else` branch (reached for computed fields, after every other `DecoratorInfo` subtype has been ruled out by the preceding `elif` chain) contained:

```python
isinstance(var_value, ComputedFieldInfo)
```

as a bare statement. The boolean result is computed and immediately discarded, so this line has no effect at all — not even for static type narrowing, since a bare expression statement doesn't narrow anything for mypy/pyright. It also checks the wrong variable: `var_value` is the `PydanticDescriptorProxy` itself, not its `.decorator_info` — so even if the result *were* used, this specific check would always evaluate to `False`.

## Fix

```python
assert isinstance(info, ComputedFieldInfo)
```

This checks the right variable (`info`, the actual `DecoratorInfo`) and turns the no-op into a real invariant check, matching the same style already used a few lines above at `PydanticDescriptorProxy.__post_init__` (line 186: `isinstance(self.decorator_info, ComputedFieldInfo)`).

Right now this branch really can only be reached with a `ComputedFieldInfo`, so nothing changes for any current input. The value is defensive: if a `DecoratorInfo` subtype is ever added without updating this `elif` chain to match, this now fails fast with a clear `AssertionError` at class-creation time, instead of silently filing it under `res.computed_fields` and surfacing a confusing `AttributeError` much later, deep inside `update_from_config`.

Small and mechanical enough that I went straight to a PR per the template's "unless your change is trivial" note — happy to open an issue first instead if you'd rather discuss it there.

## Testing

Full suite: 6110 passed, 1 pre-existing failure (`test_generic_model_pickle_different_module`, a subprocess/cloudpickle environment issue) reproduced identically on `main` with this change reverted, so unrelated to this diff.

title: Always pop field name and model type stacks during schema generation
body:
## Change Summary

`_FieldNameStack.push()` and `_ModelTypeStack.push()` appended to the stack, yielded, then popped, with no `try`/`finally`. If schema generation raised inside the `with` block and the error was caught further up (for example a custom `__get_pydantic_core_schema__` that tries `handler.generate_schema(...)` and falls back on `PydanticSchemaGenerationError`), the entry was never popped and leaked into the rest of the build.

In practice this means that after such a fallback, a later `Self` annotation in the same model resolves to the wrong class (the stale entry from the failed build), and `handler.field_name` returns a stale field name.

The fix wraps the `yield` in `try`/`finally` for both stacks, the same way `_Definitions.get_definition_ref_schema()` already does.

Added two regression tests in `tests/test_edge_cases.py` (one per stack). Both fail on `main` and pass with this change. Full test suite, `ruff`, and the pre-commit typecheck hook pass locally.

title: fix: reject non-positive multiple_of constraints with PydanticUserError
body:
## Change Summary

Reject non-positive `multiple_of` values (`<= 0`) by raising a `PydanticUserError` during field definition and schema construction, preventing uncatchable `pyo3_runtime.PanicException` crashes or division-by-zero errors at validation time.

### Problem
`Field(multiple_of=0)` was previously accepted when defining a model class, but validating any integer against it panicked inside pydantic-core with `attempt to calculate the remainder with a divisor of zero`. Because `PanicException` inherits from `BaseException` rather than `Exception`, standard validation try/except blocks (`except ValidationError`, `except Exception`) failed to catch it, causing worker processes to crash. Additionally, JSON Schema specifies that `multipleOf` must be strictly greater than zero.

### Root Cause
1. `pydantic/fields.py:FieldInfo.__init__` accepted `multiple_of` without range validation.
2. `pydantic/_internal/_known_annotated_metadata.py:apply_known_metadata` copied `multiple_of` directly into the core schema for numeric types without checking that `value > 0`.
3. `pydantic/experimental/pipeline.py:_apply_constraint` similarly allowed non-positive `multiple_of` values without validation.

### Fix
- In `pydantic/fields.py`: raise `PydanticUserError('`multiple_of` must be greater than 0')` if `multiple_of <= 0`.
- In `pydantic/_internal/_known_annotated_metadata.py`: raise `PydanticUserError` in `apply_known_metadata` if `multiple_of <= 0`.
- In `pydantic/experimental/pipeline.py`: validate that `multiple_of > 0` before applying constraint.
- In `tests/test_fields.py`: added parametrized test coverage for `0`, `0.0`, `-1`, and `-5.5` across `Field(multiple_of=...)` and `Annotated[int, MultipleOf(...)]`.

## Related issue number

Fixes #13860

title: fix(json_schema): serialization mode schema respects serialize_by_alias config
body:
## Summary

`model_json_schema(mode='serialization')` unconditionally used `serialization_alias` regardless of the `serialize_by_alias` setting. This made the schema contradict the actual `model_dump()` output when `serialize_by_alias=False` (the default since v2.11):

```python
class Model(BaseModel):
    my_field: str = Field(serialization_alias='myAlias')

Model(my_field='x').model_dump()               # {'my_field': 'x'}  ← field name
Model.model_json_schema(mode='serialization')  # {'myAlias': ...}   ← alias (BUG)
```

The validation path in `_get_alias_name` already gates on `validate_by_alias`. The serialization path was missing the equivalent check.

## Fix

One-line change in `pydantic/json_schema.py` (`_get_alias_name`):

```python
# before
alias = field.get('serialization_alias', name)

# after
alias = name if not self._config.serialize_by_alias else field.get('serialization_alias', name)
```

## Tests

- Updates `test_validate_by_alias_false_uses_the_field_name` to reflect the corrected default behaviour (serialization schema now matches `model_dump()` defaults).
- Adds `test_serialization_schema_respects_serialize_by_alias` with two cases:
  1. Default (`serialize_by_alias=False`): schema and `model_dump()` both use field name.
  2. `serialize_by_alias=True`: schema and `model_dump()` both use alias.

Fixes #13754

title: fix(create_model): accept PydanticDescriptorProxy in __validators__ type annotation
body:
## Summary

`model_validator()` returns `PydanticDescriptorProxy[ModelValidatorDecoratorInfo]`, not a plain `Callable`. Passing the result to `create_model()`'s `__validators__` parameter works at runtime but produces a type-checker error because the annotation only accepts `Callable[..., Any]`:

```python
@model_validator(mode='after')
def check_positive(self: 'MyModel') -> 'MyModel':
    ...

# TypeError reported by Mypy/Pyright/Pyrefly:
MyModel = create_model('MyModel', value=(int, ...), __validators__={'check_positive': check_positive})
```

## Fix

Widen the `__validators__` annotation in all three overloads (both `@overload` stubs and the concrete implementation) to also accept `PydanticDescriptorProxy[Any]`:

```python
# before
__validators__: dict[str, Callable[..., Any]] | None = None

# after
__validators__: dict[str, Callable[..., Any] | _decorators.PydanticDescriptorProxy[Any]] | None = None
```

`_decorators` is already imported in `main.py`, so no new import is needed.

## Test

Adds `test_create_model_model_validator_in_validators` to `tests/test_create_model.py` confirming:
- runtime validation fires correctly
- type checkers see no error

Fixes #13834

title: Respect the propagated `extra` config in the JSON Schema of stdlib dataclasses
body:
## Change Summary

Configuration is propagated to stdlib dataclasses that don't set their own. Validation does this; #10928 fixed it in the core-schema generator. The JSON-schema generator never followed: `GenerateJsonSchema.dataclass_schema` still reads only `getattr(cls, '__pydantic_config__', {})`.

So with a parent `extra='forbid'`, the nested dataclass **rejects** unknown keys but its JSON schema doesn't say `additionalProperties: false`. The schema and the validator disagree. This bites wherever the schema is handed to something that fills it in, e.g. LLM tool calling.

The fix: when the dataclass sets no `extra` of its own, `dataclass_schema` takes it from the config the validator was built with (`config.extra_fields_behavior` in the core schema). That covers a parent model and a `TypeAdapter(list[DC], config=...)` alike; in the second case the config exists only in the core schema. The dataclass's own `extra` still wins, and Pydantic dataclasses keep their own config boundary.

Tests: two cases that fail on `main` (model parent, `TypeAdapter` config), and three guards that pass before and after (own config wins, nothing configured, Pydantic dataclass boundary). This also fixes `test_dataclass_with_extra_forbid`, which configured `extra='ignore'` and so never tested `forbid`.

Locally: `tests/` (excluding `tests/pydantic_core`) gives 6126 passed. `test_generics.py::test_generic_model_pickle_different_module` fails identically on `main` in my checkout (an `IndexError` building a module path), so it's unrelated. `ruff` and `pyright` are clean.

Validation JSON schemas declared temporal fields as ISO 8601 strings while shipping a numeric `default`, producing an invalid schema:

title: Fix import of the V1 Hypothesis plugin under Pydantic V2
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! -->

## Change Summary

`pydantic/v1/_hypothesis_plugin.py` ships with Pydantic V2. But it imported the top-level names `pydantic`, `pydantic.color` and `pydantic.types`. Under V2, those names point to the V2 modules. So the V1-only names that the module reads from them (`color.r_rgba`, `types.ConstrainedNumberMeta`, `types._DEFINED_TYPES`) raised `AttributeError` at import time. The plugin could not be imported at all.

This change points the import at the V1 namespace:

    -import pydantic
    -import pydantic.color
    -import pydantic.types
    +import pydantic.v1 as pydantic

The package `pydantic.v1` already exposes `color` and `types` as attributes. So one aliased import is enough. A separate `import pydantic.v1.color` is not needed. That form would also break: `import a.b.c` without `as` binds the top-level name `pydantic` again and overwrites the alias.

## Validation

- Reproduced both CI test failures with `pydantic.generics` already loaded. The tests now filter only the known Hypothesis `GenericModel` deprecation warning.
- 53 related tests passed locally on Python 3.13. Restoring the original imports still makes both regression tests fail.

title: Make the serialization JSON schema respect serialize_by_alias
body:
Fixes #13754.

## Root cause

`GenerateJsonSchema._get_alias_name()` had three branches: computed fields, `mode='validation'`, and everything else (`mode='serialization'`). The `mode='validation'` branch was already fixed in #13717 to check `validate_by_alias` before using the alias. The `mode='serialization'` branch (and the computed-field branch) never got the equivalent treatment — they used the alias unconditionally:

```python
def _get_alias_name(self, field: CoreSchemaField, name: str) -> str:
    if field['type'] == 'computed-field':
        alias: Any = field.get('alias', name)
    elif self.mode == 'validation':
        alias = name if not self._config.validate_by_alias else field.get('validation_alias', name)
    else:
        alias = field.get('serialization_alias', name)  # <- always aliased
```

Since `serialize_by_alias` defaults to `False`, this makes `model_json_schema(mode='serialization')` key its properties by alias even when `model_dump()` on the exact same model emits the field name — the schema contradicts the very output it's supposed to describe:

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

class Model(BaseModel):
    my_field: str = Field(serialization_alias='myAlias')

m = Model(my_field='foo')
print(list(m.model_dump()))                                       # ['my_field']
print(list(Model.model_json_schema(mode='serialization')['properties']))  # ['myAlias']  <- mismatch
```

## Fix

Mirror the `mode='validation'` branch for both the `else` (serialization) branch and the computed-field branch, gating on `serialize_by_alias`:

```python
if field['type'] == 'computed-field':
    alias: Any = name if not self._config.serialize_by_alias else field.get('alias', name)
elif self.mode == 'validation':
    alias = name if not self._config.validate_by_alias else field.get('validation_alias', name)
else:
    alias = name if not self._config.serialize_by_alias else field.get('serialization_alias', name)
```

With `serialize_by_alias=True`, both `model_dump(by_alias=True)` and the serialization schema still agree on the aliased names, unchanged.

## Test updates

Two existing tests had serialization-mode assertions that were pinning the pre-fix (always-aliased) behavior — `test_validate_by_alias_false_uses_the_field_name` and `test_mode_name_causes_no_conflict`. I verified `model_dump()` on the exact models in both tests and updated the expected schema output to match it (both now assert `model_dump()`'s keys directly alongside the schema, so they can't silently drift apart again).

## Testing

- Added `test_serialization_schema_matches_dump_by_default`, covering both a plain field with `serialization_alias` and a computed field with `alias`, at both `serialize_by_alias=False` (default) and `serialize_by_alias=True`. Verified it fails on unpatched code with the exact mismatch from the issue, and passes with the fix.
- `pytest tests/test_json_schema.py` — 652 passed, 5 skipped, 1 xfailed (no failures, no changes from before this PR).
- `pytest tests/ --ignore=tests/pydantic_core` — 6072 passed (vs. 6071 on `main`, the +1 being the new test); the 38 pre-existing failures under `tests/type*` are identical on `main` without this change (a `pydantic-core` API/version mismatch in my local environment, unrelated to this diff — confirmed by running the exact same command against unpatched `main`).
- `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` — clean.

title: Fix RootModel equality with type aliases
body:
## Change Summary

`RootModel.__eq__` compared `root` field annotations with identity/equality of the annotation objects. A PEP 695 / `TypeAliasType` alias is a different object than the type it aliases, so:

```python
from pydantic import RootModel

type SomeStr = str

assert RootModel[str]("a") == RootModel[str]("a")
assert RootModel[str]("a") == RootModel[SomeStr]("a")  # previously failed
```

This PR still compares root annotations (as in #5948), but unwraps `TypeAliasType` / PEP 695 aliases via `__value__` first. Aliases of the same type compare equal; distinct parametrizations stay unequal:

- `RootModel[str]("a") == RootModel[SomeStr]("a")`
- `RootModel[int](42) != RootModel[float](42)`
- `RootModel[Any](1) != RootModel[int](1)`

`super().__eq__` still checks generic origin types, field values, and private attributes.

title: Derive alias config on a copy, not in the caller's ConfigDict
body:
Discussion in #13786 — deliberately not using a closing keyword, since I am not assigned to it.

### The bug

Two models that declare the same configuration and the same field validate differently, depending on what a base class declared:

```python
class Parent(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(populate_by_name=True)
    p: int = 0

class Child(Parent):
    model_config = ConfigDict(populate_by_name=False)
    x: int = Field(alias='X')

class Standalone(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(populate_by_name=False)
    x: int = Field(alias='X')

Standalone(x=1)  # ValidationError, alias required
Child(x=1)       # Child(p=0, x=1)  -- alias requirement silently bypassed
```

### Cause

`core_config()` patches the deprecated settings into their replacements by writing into `self.config_dict`, which is the very mapping it was given:

```python
config = self.config_dict
...
if config.get('validate_by_name') is None:
    config['validate_by_alias'] = True
    config['validate_by_name'] = populate_by_name
```

For a model that mapping is `model_config`, so a value pydantic derived ends up stored next to the ones the user declared:

```
Parent.model_config    : {'populate_by_name': True,  'validate_by_alias': True, 'validate_by_name': True}
Child.model_config     : {'populate_by_name': False, 'validate_by_alias': True, 'validate_by_name': True}
Standalone.model_config: {'populate_by_name': False, 'validate_by_alias': True, 'validate_by_name': False}
```

Subclass config is merged over the parent's, so `Child` inherits the derived `validate_by_name=True`, and the `is None` guard then declines to derive again from `Child`'s own `populate_by_name=False`. The derived value outranks the explicit one.

`docs/concepts/config.md` describes `model_config` as the merge of what was declared, and its inheritance example prints exactly the keys the user set — so this is also what the documented merge is defined over.

The same write reaches user-owned mappings through the direct-config entry points, where `config_dict` really is the caller's object:

```
TypeAdapter(config=...)   : before {'populate_by_name': True} after {..., 'validate_by_alias': True, 'validate_by_name': True}
validate_call(config=...) : before {'populate_by_name': True} after {..., 'validate_by_alias': True, 'validate_by_name': True}
@dataclass(config=...)    : same
```

### Fix

Derive on a copy. The derived values are only ever read back by `core_config` itself on the way to `CoreConfig`: the sole runtime reader of either name outside this function is `json_schema.py:1659`, and it reads `validate_by_alias`, which the patch only ever sets to `True` — already the default. So nothing downstream sees a change.

### The one existing test this changes

`test_dynamic_default` asserted the derived value was visible on `model_config`:

```python
assert Model.model_config == {'validate_by_alias': False, 'validate_by_name': True}
```

That assertion and correct merging cannot both hold. While `model_config` is a plain dict there is nothing to distinguish a derived value from a declared one, so anything stored there participates in the merge and wins over a subclass's explicit setting. The test now asserts the derived default is *applied* — `Model(a=1)` works and `{'A': 1}` is rejected — rather than where it is kept, which is what it was really about.

If you would rather keep it visible and re-derive during the merge instead, I am glad to rework it that way; that route needs a way to mark derived keys, which seemed like your call to make rather than mine.

### Tests

- `test_dynamic_default` — rewritten as above.
- `test_derived_alias_config_is_not_inherited_as_explicit` — `Child` and `Standalone` must validate identically.
- `test_config_argument_is_not_mutated` — `TypeAdapter`, `validate_call` and `@dataclass` leave the caller's `ConfigDict` alone.

Full suite (`pytest tests/ --ignore=tests/benchmarks`): **5864 passed, 226 skipped, 4 failed** — the same 4 failures the tree has without this change (`test_validate_call.py:262`, `test_json_schema.py:1025`, `test_main.py:1442`, `test_types.py:3182`), so no new failures.

Reverting only `_config.py` and keeping the tests fails exactly the three above, 83 others in `test_config.py` passing either way.

A note on how that was run: `main` currently imports `_schema_gather` from `pydantic-core`, which the published 2.48.0 wheel does not export, so the suite cannot run against a released core. I ran it at `585c994~1` (the commit before "Move schema gathering logic to `pydantic-core`"), where `_config.py` and `tests/test_config.py` are byte-identical to `main` — `git diff main 585c994~1 --` on both files is empty.

title: Fix Field metadata (examples, deprecated, title) lost in RootModel JSON schema
body:
## Summary

When a `RootModel` declares the `root` field with `Field(examples=..., deprecated=True, title=...)`, those attributes are silently dropped from the generated JSON schema. Only `description` and `json_schema_extra` were being propagated.

- Propagate `examples` from `root` field to the JSON schema output
- Propagate `deprecated` from `root` field to the JSON schema output
- Propagate `title` from `root` field as a fallback before using the class name

The fix is in `_update_class_schema` in `json_schema.py`, following the same pattern already used for `description` on line 1670.

Closes #11922

## Reproduction

```python
from typing import Annotated
from pydantic import RootModel, Field

class Foo(RootModel):
    root: Annotated[str, Field(examples=['foo', 'bar'], deprecated=True)]

print(Foo.model_json_schema())
# Before: {'title': 'Foo', 'type': 'string'}
# After:  {'deprecated': True, 'examples': ['foo', 'bar'], 'title': 'Foo', 'type': 'string'}
```

## Test plan

- `uv run python -m pytest tests/test_root_model.py tests/test_json_schema.py -x -q`
- Added 5 new targeted tests covering `examples`, `deprecated`, `title`, config title override, and combined usage

title: Buffer one-shot iterator input during union validation
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! -->
<!-- Unless your change is trivial, please create an issue to discuss the change before creating a PR -->

## Change Summary

Validating a one-shot iterator (e.g. a generator) against a union of sequences silently dropped the items consumed by a failed member before trying the next one. This PR wraps iterator input in a new `TeeIterable` type, which buffers consumed items and lets each union member re-iterate from the start, in both `smart` and `left_to_right` modes.

Buffering is lazy: items are only recorded as members consume them, and non-iterator inputs are completely unaffected (a single `isinstance` check on the input). Unlike the approach in #12790, nothing is eagerly materialized.

Known limitation: iterators *nested* inside the union input (e.g. a model field holding a generator, as pointed out in https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/pull/12790#issuecomment-2649000000) still lose consumed data, since member validation receives the raw iterator. Fixing that case would require threading validation state into `Input::validate_*` methods, which I'd be happy to explore as a follow-up if the approach here looks reasonable.

title: Support type alias to None or MISSING in discriminated unions
body:
Discussion in #13781 — deliberately not using a closing keyword as I am not assigned to the issue yet.

### Description
When a member of a discriminated union is a type alias resolving to `None` (or `MISSING`), schema building fails with:
`TypeError: The core schema type 'none' is not a valid discriminated union variant.`

This happens because `_handle_choice()` was not inspecting the dereferenced schema of `definition-ref` choices to detect `none`, `nullable`, or `missing-sentinel` targets before attempting to infer discriminator values.

### Changes

title: Fix TypeError instead of using fallback when __pydantic_serializer__ …
body:
Fix TypeError instead of using fallback when __pydantic_serializer__ attribute is not a SchemaSerializer

Objects with a `__getattr__` that never raises `AttributeError` (e.g. `unittest.mock.call`) get classified as `ObType::PydanticSerializable` because `hasattr(value, '__pydantic_serializer__')` returns `True`, even though the attribute isn't actually a `SchemaSerializer` instance. Previously this raised a bare `TypeError` from `serialize_pydantic_serializable`, bypassing any user-provided fallback. Now it falls through to the same handling as `ObType::Unknown` (fallback, then `serialize_unknown`, then error).

## Change Summary

`serialize_pydantic_serializable` now checks whether the `__pydantic_serializer__` attribute actually downcasts to a `SchemaSerializer` before calling it. If the downcast fails, serialization falls through to the existing unknown-type handling instead of raising immediately, so a user-supplied `fallback` is respected.

Fixes #13734

body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! -->
<!-- Unless your change is trivial, please create an issue to discuss the change before creating a PR -->

## Change Summary

Fixes https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/issues/13017, fixes https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/issues/13089.

While this PR fixes the two reported issues, it also makes the pattern opt-in, because the pattern is quite complex still, and could cause issues downstream. There's also a chance that we have to tweak it in the future (e.g. fix other edge cases, adapting to new accepted string input by `Decimal` in future Python versions). By making it opt-in, we can make changes way more easily, without worrying about "breaking" (in the sense that the JSON Schema would unconditionally change for users). If users opt in for the pattern, they accept the pattern to change.

As we underestimated the impact of JSON Schema to downstream users (or at least underestimated the number of users relying on the JSON Schema for validation purposes), we should probably be more careful about such changes, and potentially define a policy for such changes (e.g. no changes between minor releases).

title: Add pipeline API
body:
This PR introduces a new experimental API to do more type-safe advanced constraining, parsing and transformation of types.

```python
from typing import Annotated
from pydantic import BaseModel, validate_as, transform

class User(BaseModel):
    username: Annotated[str, transform(str.lower)]
    age: Annotated[int, validate_as().gt(0)]
```

More specifically, from the docs updates:

This PR introduces an experimental "pipeline" API that allows composing of parsing (validation), constraints and transformations in a more type-safe manner than existing APIs. This API is subject to change or removal, we are looking for feedback and suggestions before making it a permanent part of Pydantic.

Generally, the pipeline API is used to define a sequence of steps to apply to incoming data during validation. The pipeline API is designed to be more type-safe and composable than the existing Pydantic API.

Each step in the pipeline can be:
* A validation step that runs pydantic validation on the provided type
* A transformation step that modifies the data
* A constraint step that checks the data against a condition
* A predicate step that checks the data against a condition and raises an error if it returns `False`

You can see more detail in the docs here: https://transform.pydantic-docs.pages.dev/concepts/experimental/#importing-experimental-feature-warnings 

Also, this PR is very much aligned with [PEP 746](https://pep-previews--3785.org.readthedocs.build/pep-0746/), which introduces type checking for annotated metadata.

Fix #9522

^^ adding new experimental feature pattern docs to the version policy

title: Document that val_json_bytes applies in Python mode

## Change Summary

`val_json_bytes` is documented as "the encoding of JSON serialized bytes to decode", which reads as if it only applies to `validate_json`. It applies to any `str` input, so `TypeAdapter(bytes, config={'val_json_bytes': 'base64'}).validate_python('abc')` decodes rather than accepting the string as-is — and where the string happens to be valid base64 that is silently wrong rather than an error.

`docs/api/standard_library_types.md` already carries the "despite its name" note since #12287; this adds it to the `ConfigDict.val_json_bytes` reference, which is where people land from the config, and gives a short example.

The same bullet in `standard_library_types.md` says strings *and* `bytearray` instances are decoded following the setting. Only strings are:

```python
from pydantic import TypeAdapter

ta = TypeAdapter(bytes, config={'val_json_bytes': 'base64'})
ta.validate_python('YWJj')             # b'abc'
ta.validate_python(bytearray(b'YWJj')) # b'YWJj'
ta.validate_python(b'YWJj')            # b'YWJj'
```

So I split that bullet in two. Happy to drop that part if you would rather keep this to the config reference.

title: fix: respect MRO when base merely inherits a field or private attribute (#13678)
body:
## Problem

In multiple inheritance hierarchies with Pydantic models, when one base class merely inherits a field or private attribute from a common ancestor without re-declaring it, and another base class explicitly overrides that field/private attribute, the merely-inheriting base improperly shadows the override depending on base order (e.g. `Swapped(Plain, Override)` where `Plain(Base)` declares `pass` and `Override(Base)` overrides `f`).

This violates Python's Method Resolution Order (MRO), where the first class in the MRO defining an attribute in its own namespace should take precedence.

## Root Cause

Two separate lookup mechanisms were affected:
1. In `pydantic._internal._fields.collect_model_fields`, `parent_fields_lookup` was built by iterating `reversed(bases)` and updating with each base's flattened `__pydantic_fields__`. Because a base that merely inherits a field re-exposes its ancestor's `FieldInfo` in `__pydantic_fields__`, an earlier base in `bases` would overwrite an explicit override declared on a later base.
2. In `pydantic._internal._model_construction.ModelMetaclass._collect_bases_data`, `private_attributes` was built by iterating `bases` forward and updating with each base's flattened `__private_attributes__`. This caused the last base to win instead of the MRO-earliest declarer (also causing issue #11700 where `C(A, B)` took `B`'s private attribute instead of `A`'s).

## Solution

1. In `collect_model_fields`:
   - Inspect parent classes along `cls.__mro__[1:]` in forward order to identify the MRO-winning declarer for each field (`name in safe_get_annotations(base)`).
   - If an intervening parameterized generic submodel specialized that declarer (e.g. `Model[int]`), copy the specialized `FieldInfo` from that submodel so concrete type arguments are preserved.
   - If no generic specialization occurred, copy the `FieldInfo` from the winning declarer.
2. In `_collect_bases_data`:
   - Walk `reversed(mro_for_bases(bases))` and filter inherited private attributes using an ancestor identity check (`_is_declared`). Because a class that merely inherits a private attribute re-exposes an identical `ModelPrivateAttr` object from its ancestor's `__dict__`, only newly assigned private attributes count as declarations, ensuring the MRO-earliest declarer wins.

## Testing

Added comprehensive regression tests in `tests/test_edge_cases.py`:
- `test_multiple_inheritance_merely_inherited_field_does_not_shadow_override`: Directly reproduces #13678, asserting that both fields and private attributes resolve to `'override'` for both `Swapped(Plain, Override)` and `Composed(Override, Plain)`. (Fails pre-fix on `Swapped.f` and `Composed._knob`, passes post-fix).
- `test_multiple_inheritance_mro_adversarial_cases`: Adversarial coverage including:
  - Both bases declaring the same field and private attribute (#11700).
  - Deep pass-through inheritance chains (`Grandparent -> Parent -> Child` mixed with `GrandparentOverride`).
  - Diamond inheritance hierarchies.
  - Parameterized generic submodels with multiple inheritance and direct generic subclassing with type substitution and `ValidationError` enforcement.

## Verification

- Targeted: `pytest tests/test_edge_cases.py -k test_multiple_inheritance` (2 passed).
- Module: `pytest tests/test_edge_cases.py` (197 passed, 1 skipped).
- Integration: `pytest tests/test_private_attributes.py tests/test_generics.py tests/test_main.py tests/test_fields.py tests/test_construction.py` (518 passed, 27 skipped, 5 xfailed).
- Repro script: 4/4 assertions pass.

## Impact

Fields and private attributes in multiple inheritance now consistently follow Python's MRO. Single-inheritance and existing multi-inheritance models without competing inherited fields are unaffected.

## Compatibility

Backwards compatible. Closes #13678 and aligns with #11700.

title: Report string-only constraints applied to `bytes` instead of silently ignoring them
body:
## Change Summary

`Annotated[bytes, StringConstraints(pattern=...)]` (and `to_lower`, `to_upper`, `strip_whitespace`, `ascii_only`) builds without complaint and then validates nothing:

```python
TypeAdapter(Annotated[bytes, StringConstraints(pattern='^ZZZZ$')]).validate_python(b'abcde')
#> b'abcde'          # on main; the same annotation on `str` raises string_pattern_mismatch
```

`CONSTRAINTS_TO_ALLOWED_SCHEMAS` pairs `STR_CONSTRAINTS` with `TEXT_SCHEMA_TYPES`, which contains `'bytes'`, so the constraint is written onto the `bytes` core schema — which implements none of them — and dropped. The constraint is also absent from the emitted JSON Schema, so nothing downstream shows it either.

The fix pairs `STR_CONSTRAINTS` with the schema types that implement them, so these fall through to the existing report path: `RuntimeError: Unable to apply constraint 'pattern' to schema of type 'bytes'`, the same message `Annotated[list[int], Field(pattern='abc')]` already produces. `min_length`, `max_length` and `strict` on `bytes` are unaffected — they come from `BYTES_CONSTRAINTS`.

- **The one-line version of this fix is not enough, and I checked.** With only the pairing changed, these route into the `str_schema(...)` chain fallback, which in lax mode *decodes* bytes: `to_lower` on a `bytes` field then returns `'abc'` — a `str`. `ascii_only` gives `TypeError: str_schema() got an unexpected keyword argument 'ascii_only'`. Hence the second half of the change. Run against the added tests, that one-line variant fails 5 of them.
- **Origin.** `TEXT_SCHEMA_TYPES` arrived in #5883 as the dispatch list for *length* constraints, where `bytes` belongs; #6951 reused it as the allow-list for *all* string constraints while, three lines later, giving `bytes` its own narrower `BYTES_CONSTRAINTS` loop. Two answers to "what does `bytes` accept" in one file, and the wider one wins by union.
- **Why the suite doesn't catch it.** `test_invalid_schema_constraints` is the table for exactly this class of mistake, and it has rows for `int`, `list[int]`, `set`, `frozenset`, `Decimal` and `float` — no `bytes` row. Across `tests/`, `StringConstraints` and `bytes` never appear together.
- **Left alone:** `min_length` is likewise declared for `'url'`/`'multi-host-url'`, which don't implement it, but it isn't reachable through the public URL types (their schema is `function-wrap`, so it takes the functional-validator path and works).

Behaviour change: code that passes one of these constraints on a `bytes` field gets an error where it previously got silence. That code was already not being validated.

## Related issue number

None — I didn't find an existing issue for this (searched open and closed). Happy to open one first if you'd prefer that order.
