title: Add `polymorphic_serialization` option
body:
## Change Summary

(Imported from pydantic/pydantic-core#1881)

Introduced as a possible solution to #12382; the theory is that most uses of serialize_as_any are because users want to respect subtyping properly.

This PR introduces a configuration option and runtime flag polymorphic_serialization which is used to enable serializing subclasses of models and dataclasses as the subclass, not as the base class.

To maintain backwards compatibility, the default is `False` - models and dataclasses will be serialized as the exact type in the schema.

When the config is set to `True`, then models and dataclasess will be serialized as their runtime type. This also respects any model serializer the subclass may be using.

Users can also pass `polymorphic_serialization` as a runtime option to the serialization functions; doing so will override the config value (i.e. can be globally enabled or disabled).

----

## Points of Discussion for this PR

### `Annotated` metadata

Not explored yet in this PR, an additional / alternative possibility could be to expose this as some kind of wrapper so that for foreign types one can use `Annotated[ForeignModel, PolymorphicSerialization]` to enable this even when the type didn't opt in.

(An `Annotated` form may remove the need for the global runtime override.)

### Non-Pydantic types

This method cannot really ever work for types which Pydantic doesn't know how to serialize, e.g. subclass of `int` will _not_ be serialized polymorphically. If the subclass had a `__pydantic_serializer__` attribute it could in theory work, but I think that's the _unlikely_ case.

More complicated is stdlib dataclasses and `TypedDict`. It might be reasonable to expect these to work, but I think that would require inspection of the subclass types at runtime and somehow caching a serializer for them. (i.e. a lot of runtime callback into `Pydantic`.)

### Backwards compatibility

For the concern listed above on non-pydantic types, one way to introduce support for them later would be to have the runtime flag accept a set of types to serialize, e.g. `polymorphic_serialization = {BaseModel, BaseDataClass, int}`

... but another way to avoid the problem entirely would be to not have the global runtime flag and use the `Annotated` form to apply this behavior only to supported types.

## Related issue number

#12382

title: Allow default factories of private attributes to take validated model data
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! -->
<!-- Unless your change is trivial, please create an issue to discuss the change before creating a PR -->

## Change Summary

<!-- Please give a short summary of the changes. -->

This PR adds `default_factory` to `PrivateAttr` working in a similar way that it works with `Field`. Due that private attributes happen after init, the `default_factory` callable has available the entire `__dict__` attribute. Also, private attributes defined **before** the current private are available (similar as this callable work with field)

```python
class Model(BaseModel):
    x: str
    _y: str = PrivateAttr(default = 'y')
    _z: str = PrivateAttr(default_factory = lambda data: data['x'] + data['_y'] + 'z')
    
m =  Model(x = 'x')
>>> m._z
'xyz'

# Fails with KeyError

class Model(BaseModel):
    x: str
    _y: str = PrivateAttr(default_factory= lambda data: data['x'] + data['_z'] + 'y')
    _z: str = PrivateAttr(default = 'z')

Model(x = 'x')
>>> KeyError

```

When using `-p /other/project <command>`, PDM was always loading
`[tool.pdm.options]` from the current working directory instead of the
target project. This meant default options (e.g. `no_sync = true`) in
the target project's `pyproject.toml` were silently ignored.

**Root causes:**

1. `_get_cli_args()` called `create_project(is_global=False)` with no
   path, so it always read options from cwd regardless of `-p`.

2. `get_command()` didn't know that `-p`/`--project` consumes a value
   argument. With `pdm -p /path install`, it would find `/path` as the
   subcommand name and fail to look up `install` in the options table.

**Fix:**

- Added `_get_project_path_from_args()` — a lightweight pre-parse that
  extracts the `-p`/`--project` value from raw args before full
  argument parsing.
- `_get_cli_args()` now passes that path to `create_project()` so
  `[tool.pdm.options]` is loaded from the correct project.
- Added `"-p"` and `"--project"` to `options_with_values` in
  `get_command()` so the subcommand is identified correctly when a
  project path is given.

With versions of the `uuid` crate prior to 1.23.0, the existing `test_uuid` works, matching the entire error message for input `'not-a-valid-uuid'`:

https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/blob/ac249284616890d91c746dc890fb0f6407df2843/pydantic-core/tests/validators/test_uuid.py#L40-L47

With `uuid` version 1.23.0, the error message text changes, causing the test to fail:

[…]

        if isinstance(expected, Err):
            with pytest.raises(ValidationError, match=re.escape(expected.message)):
>               result = v.validate_python(input_value)
                         ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
E               pydantic_core._pydantic_core.ValidationError: 1 validation error for uuid
E                 Input should be a valid UUID, invalid character: found `n` at 1 [type=uuid_parsing, input_value='not-a-valid-uuid', input_type=str]
E                   For further information visit https://errors.pydantic.dev/latest/v/uuid_parsing

tests/validators/test_uuid.py:90: ValidationError

During handling of the above exception, another exception occurred:

input_value = 'not-a-valid-uuid', expected = Err('Input should be a valid UUID, invalid character: expected an optional prefix of `urn:uuid:` followed by [0-9a-fA-F-], found `n` at 1')

    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
        'input_value,expected',
        [
[…]
        ],
    )
    def test_uuid(input_value, expected):
        v = SchemaValidator(core_schema.uuid_schema())
        if isinstance(expected, Err):
>           with pytest.raises(ValidationError, match=re.escape(expected.message)):
                 ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
E           AssertionError: Regex pattern did not match.
E             Expected regex: 'Input\\ should\\ be\\ a\\ valid\\ UUID,\\ invalid\\ character:\\ expected\\ an\\ optional\\ prefix\\ of\\ `urn:uuid:`\\ followed\\ by\\ \\[0\\-9a\\-fA\\-F\\-\\],\\ found\\ `n`\\ at\\ 1'

tests/validators/test_uuid.py:89: AssertionError
```

So instead of the following *full* error output

```
1 validation error for uuid
  Input should be a valid UUID, invalid character: expected an optional prefix of `urn:uuid:` followed by [0-9a-fA-F-], found `n` at 1 [type=uuid_parsing, input_value='not-a-valid-uuid', input_type=str]

we now have

title: Add Optional Enum Key Names to JSON Schema Generation (`x-enum-varnames`)
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! -->
<!-- Unless your change is trivial, please create an issue to discuss the change before creating a PR -->

## Change Summary

The JSON Schema serializer now emits the `x-enum-varnames` array containing the enum keys when the `use_x_enum_varnames` option is specified.
This is a commonly [supported](https://openapi-generator.tech/docs/templating/#enum) vendor extension that documents the names of each of the enum members. It enables code generators for Typescript and Python to losslessly create a 1:1 representation of each-other's enums.

### Changes

- Added new boolean config option used in the JSON Schema serializer: `use_x_enum_varnames`
- Added test coverage: Test cases covering true/false/default values in he config. 

#### `include-x-enum-varnames`

**Type:** `bool`

True if the generated JSON Schema enums should have the `x-enum-varnames` extension emitted.
This maintains the key of any enum value that is defined in the form `key = 'value'`.
The default behavior is to use the value as both the key and value.

Default: `False`

### Example

```python
from enum import Enum

from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict

class SomeEnum(Enum):
    FOO = 'foo'
    BAR = 'bar'
    BAZ = 'baz'

class DefaultModel(BaseModel):
    value: SomeEnum

DefaultModel.model_json_schema()['$defs']['SomeEnum']
# "SomeEnum": {
#     "enum": ["foo", "bar", "baz"],
#     "title": "SomeEnum",
#     "type": "string"
# }

class VarnamesModel(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(use_x_enum_varnames=True)
    value: SomeEnum

VarnamesModel.model_json_schema()['$defs']['SomeEnum']
# {
#     'enum': ['foo', 'bar', 'baz'],
#     'title': 'SomeEnum',
#     'type': 'string',
#     'x-enum-varnames': ['FOO', 'BAR', 'BAZ'],
# }
```

title: Box large fields in CombinedValidator/CombinedSerializer to reduce enum size
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! -->
<!-- Unless your change is trivial, please create an issue to discuss the change before creating a PR -->

## Change Summary

Box large inline fields (`LiteralLookup`, `Discriminator`, `AHashSet`) in the largest `CombinedValidator` and `CombinedSerializer` variants to reduce memory consumption.

### Why?
The hint was given in https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/issues/12272#issuecomment-3339381316.
Rust enums are sized to their largest variant. `TaggedUnionValidator` was 448 bytes, inflating every node in the validator to 448 bytes. Models with many fields create hundreds of nodes, so this adds up. Boxing moves the large data to the heap (8-byte pointer), shrinking `CombinedValidator` from 448 → 192 bytes (57%) and `CombinedSerializer` from 248 → 136 bytes (45%).

The total memory consumption reduction is around 10%.

More details in https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/issues/12272.

### Full comparison:
``` bash
CombinedValidator                   448 B  →     192 B  (57% reduction)
Variant                            Before      After      Delta
------------------------------ ---------- ---------- ----------
TaggedUnionValidator                448 B      176 B       -272
StrEnumValidator                    320 B      104 B       -216
PlainEnumValidator                  320 B      104 B       -216
IntEnumValidator                    320 B      104 B       -216
FloatEnumValidator                  320 B      104 B       -216
LiteralValidator                    272 B       56 B       -216
UrlValidator                        184 B      184 B          -
MultiHostUrlValidator               184 B      184 B          -
ConstrainedIntValidator             168 B      168 B          -
UnionValidator                      136 B      136 B          -
...


CombinedSerializer                  248 B  →     136 B  (45% reduction)
Variant                            Before      After      Delta
------------------------------ ---------- ---------- ----------
TypedDictSerializer                 240 B      128 B       -112
GeneralFieldsSerializer             240 B      128 B       -112
TupleSerializer                     192 B       80 B       -112
DictSerializer                      168 B       56 B       -112
LiteralSerializer                   160 B       48 B       -112
ListSerializer                      160 B       48 B       -112
TaggedUnionSerializer               152 B       96 B        -56
GeneratorSerializer                 136 B       24 B       -112
FunctionWrapSerializer               80 B       80 B          -
FunctionPlainSerializer              80 B       80 B          -
DataclassSerializer                  64 B       64 B          -
...
```

title: Fix PydanticOmit not caught in definitions_schema for shared types
body:
## Summary

Fixes #12706

When a type that raises `PydanticOmit` in `__get_pydantic_json_schema__` is
referenced in multiple fields (e.g., in union types), pydantic-core moves it
into a shared `definitions` section of the CoreSchema. `definitions_schema()`
catches `PydanticInvalidForJsonSchema` for definitions but did not catch
`PydanticOmit`, causing it to propagate as an unhandled exception.

## Fix

Follows the exact same pattern already established for `PydanticInvalidForJsonSchema`:

1. **Track omitted definitions** — new `_core_defs_omitted_for_json_schema: set[DefsRef]`
2. **Catch at definition time** — `definitions_schema()` now catches `PydanticOmit`
3. **Re-raise at reference time** — `definition_ref_schema()` checks if the ref was omitted
4. **Propagate through helpers** — `get_schema_from_definitions()` and `_add_json_refs()` also check
5. **Clear on populate** — if a definition is later successfully populated, the omitted flag is cleared

## Changes

- **`pydantic/json_schema.py`**: 5 locations modified, all following the existing
  `PydanticInvalidForJsonSchema` pattern

}

strum::ParseError::VariantNotFound
}

#[strum(parse_error_ty = strum::ParseError, parse_error_fn = make_error)]

    Red,
    #[strum(default)]
    Other(String),
}

    fn make_error(x: &str) -> strum::ParseError {
strum::ParseError::VariantNotFound
}

  • #474: EnumDiscriminants will now copy default over from the original enum to the Discriminant enum.

    #[derive(Debug, Default, EnumDiscriminants)]
#[strum_discriminants(derive(Default))] // <- Remove this in 0.28.
enum MyEnum {
    #[default] // <- Will be the #[default] on the MyEnumDiscriminant
    #[strum_discriminants(default)] // <- Remove this in 0.28
    Variant0,
    Variant1 { a: NonDefault },

title: Add support for __root__ key in RootModel exclude/include parameters
body:
## Description

This PR implements support for the `__root__` key in `exclude` and `include` parameters when calling `model_dump()` or `model_dump_json()` on a `RootModel` instance.

Fixes https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/discussions/11383

## Problem

As reported in [Discussion #11383](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/discussions/11383), there was no straightforward syntax to exclude/include fields from nested models when using `RootModel[list[Model]]` or similar structures. Users wanted a way to filter fields from items within the root value without having to use `Field(exclude=True)`.

## Solution

The implementation introduces support for the `__root__` key in exclude/include dictionaries. When a user specifies `__root__` in the parameter, it applies filtering to items within the root value.

### Key Changes

1. **Modified `pydantic/root_model.py`**:
   - Added `_process_include_exclude()` method that transforms `__root__` keys
   - Overrode `model_dump()` and `model_dump_json()` methods to process the `__root__` key before serialization
   - When `__root__` is specified, its value is extracted and used directly since RootModel serializes to its root value

2. **Added comprehensive tests in `tests/test_root_model.py`**:
   - 9 test functions covering various use cases
   - Tests for both `exclude` and `include` parameters
   - Tests for list-based and dict-based RootModels
   - Tests for `__all__` keyword and specific indices/keys

## Usage Examples

### Exclude field from all list items
```python
from pydantic import BaseModel, RootModel

class Foo(BaseModel):
    a: int
    b: int | None = None

TestModel = RootModel[list[Foo]]
instance = TestModel([Foo(a=1, b=2), Foo(a=3, b=4)])

# Exclude 'b' from all items
result = instance.model_dump(exclude={'__root__': {'__all__': {'b'}}})
# Result: [{'a': 1}, {'a': 3}]
```

### Include only specific fields
```python
# Include only 'a' from all items
result = instance.model_dump(include={'__root__': {'__all__': {'a'}}})
# Result: [{'a': 1}, {'a': 3}]
```

### Exclude from specific index
```python
# Exclude 'b' from first item only
result = instance.model_dump(exclude={'__root__': {0: {'b'}}})
# Result: [{'a': 1}, {'a': 3, 'b': 4}]
```

### Works with dict-based RootModels
```python
DictModel = RootModel[dict[str, Foo]]
instance = DictModel({'first': Foo(a=1, b=2), 'second': Foo(a=3, b=4)})

# Exclude 'b' from all dict values
result = instance.model_dump(exclude={'__root__': {'__all__': {'b'}}})
# Result: {'first': {'a': 1}, 'second': {'a': 3}}
```

## Design Decisions

1. **Consistent with `__all__` pattern**: The implementation follows the existing pattern of using `__all__` for applying operations to all items in a collection
2. **Non-breaking**: The change is fully backwards compatible
3. **Intuitive API**: The `__root__` key makes semantic sense for `RootModel` where the root field contains the actual data
4. **Symmetric support**: Works identically for both `exclude` and `include` parameters

## Testing

All 9 new tests pass successfully, covering:
- List-based RootModels with `__all__` and specific indices
- Dict-based RootModels with `__all__` and specific keys  
- Both `exclude` and `include` parameters
- Both `model_dump()` and `model_dump_json()` methods
- The original example from the GitHub discussion

## Checklist

- [x] Implementation complete
- [x] Tests added and passing
- [x] Backwards compatible
- [x] Documentation in docstrings
- [ ] Changelog entry (will add if requested)
- [ ] Documentation update (will add if requested)

title: Fix model_dump to include extra fields from __pydantic_extra__
body:
## Change Summary

fix #12937

`model_dump()` and `model_dump_json()` dropped extra fields when
`model_validate(data, extra='allow')` populated `__pydantic_extra__` on a model
whose own config is `extra='forbid'` or `extra='ignore'`.

The pydantic-core serializer only reads `__pydantic_extra__` when the schema has
`extra_behavior='allow'`. When the schema says `forbid` or `ignore`, it never
checks the attribute, so runtime extras from `model_validate` overrides are
silently lost.

The fix changes `ModelSerializer.get_inner_value` in pydantic-core to check
`__pydantic_extra__` at runtime even when `has_extra` is false. If the attribute
is populated and the model is an instance of the expected class, the extras are
passed to the serializer. The class check prevents leaking extras when a model
is serialized by a foreign serializer (e.g. Parent serializer applied to an
unrelated Other instance).

`extract_dicts` in `GeneralFieldsSerializer` now handles both tuple and plain
dict inputs, so models with runtime extras work correctly through wrapped
serializers too.

This handles nested models at all levels. Each nested model goes through its own
`ModelSerializer`, so the runtime check applies recursively.

The previous Python-level post-processing in `model_dump()`/`model_dump_json()`
is removed since the fix is now in pydantic-core.

## Related issue number

fix #12937

title: perf: skip already-processed bases in get_model_type_hints
body:
## Summary

When a base class already has `__pydantic_fields__` and all its annotation names are already collected in `hints`, skip the entire base. This avoids namespace resolver overhead for deep inheritance trees where parent fields have already been processed.

For classes with 3-7 levels of inheritance creating 10k+ unique classes, this eliminates redundant MRO traversal per class.

## Change

In `get_model_type_hints()`, added early-exit check before the `with ns_resolver.push(base):` block:
```python
base_model_fields = base.__dict__.get('__pydantic_fields__')
if base_model_fields is not None and all(name in hints for name in ann):
    continue
```
Also removed duplicate base_model_fields lookup inside the with block.

Fixes #12647

## Summary

Related to #10790.

Expands the "On inheritance" note in the validators documentation to include a clear description of the execution order when both a base class and a subclass define model validators of different modes (`before`, `after`, `wrap`).

## Changes

- Added bullet-point rules describing the validator execution order with inheritance
- Added a concrete code example showing the full execution order with output comments

The example demonstrates:
- Subclass `wrap` validators run outermost (first entry, last exit)
- Base class `wrap` validators run inside the subclass `wrap`
- `before` validators: subclass-first, then base class
- `after` validators: base class-first, then subclass

This makes explicit the behaviour reported in #10790 so users can understand and predict the ordering.

`model_validate_strings()` currently skips the custom `__init__` path for models because `StringMapping` always returns `None` from `Input::as_kwargs()`.

This causes behavior differences compared to `model_validate()` / `model_validate_json()` for models that override `__init__`, and is the root issue reported in #12718.

## Changes
- Return mapping kwargs from `StringMapping::as_kwargs()` when the input is a mapping.
- Keep `None` for non-mapping (`String`) values.
- Add regression test ensuring `model_validate_strings()` invokes a custom `__init__` and forwards string mapping values.

## Tests
- `uv run pytest tests/test_edge_cases.py -k "custom_init or model_validate_strings_custom_init_called or init_inspection"`
- `uv run pytest tests/test_main.py -k "model_validate_strings"`

Closes #12718

title: Fix pattern constraint dropped from JSON schema with Annotated BeforeValidator on Optional fields
body:
## Change Summary

When a field uses an `Annotated` type with a `BeforeValidator` and a `Field()` `pattern` constraint (e.g. `Optional[Annotated[str, BeforeValidator(fn)]] = Field(None, pattern=...)`), the `pattern` was missing from the generated JSON schema.

The root cause: `apply_known_metadata` could not directly apply `chain_schema_constraints` (like `pattern`, `strip_whitespace`, etc.) to function-type schemas (`function-before`, `function-wrap`, `function-after`). Instead, it wrapped the schema in a chain with a separate validation step containing the constraint. The JSON schema generator's `chain_schema` handler only inspects `step[0]` for validation mode, so the `pattern` in `step[1]` was lost.

The fix adds a check in `apply_known_metadata`: when the schema is a function type and the constraint is a `chain_schema_constraint`, apply it directly to the inner schema if the inner schema type supports that constraint. This ensures the constraint is both enforced at runtime (by pydantic-core) and correctly reflected in the JSON schema.

**Before:**
```python
annotated_optional:
{'anyOf': [{'type': 'string'}, {'type': 'null'}],
 'default': None,
 'title': 'Annotated Optional'}
# pattern is missing!
```

**After:**
```python
annotated_optional:
{'anyOf': [{'pattern': '^[\\da-fA-F]{32}$', 'type': 'string'}, {'type': 'null'}],
 'default': None,
 'title': 'Annotated Optional'}
```

## Related issue number

fix #12417

title: Fix model_dump not including extra fields when model_validate overrides extra to 'allow'
body:
## Change Summary

When `model_validate` is called with `extra='allow'` on a model configured with `extra='forbid'` or `extra='ignore'`, the extra fields are correctly stored in `__pydantic_extra__` but were not included in `model_dump()` or `model_dump_json()` output. This is because the serializer schema is generated at class creation time based on the class-level config, and doesn't account for per-instance extra overrides.

This fix merges `__pydantic_extra__` into the dump result after serialization, respecting `include`/`exclude` parameters.

## Related issue number

Fixes #12937

## Changes

- **pydantic/main.py**: Added `_should_include_extra_field` helper and modified `model_dump`/`model_dump_json` to merge extra fields when present
- **tests/test_main.py**: Added `test_model_validate_extra_allow_dump` covering the fix

## Example

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel

class A(BaseModel, extra='forbid'):
    a: int

a = A.model_validate({'a': 1, 'b': 'test'}, extra='allow')
print(a)              # A(a=1, b='test')
print(a.model_dump()) # {'a': 1, 'b': 'test'}  # was {'a': 1}
```

title: Handle custom $ref/$defs in __get_pydantic_json_schema__
body:
Fixes #12145

When a custom type returns a JSON schema containing $ref and $defs from __get_pydantic_json_schema__, TypeAdapter.json_schema() raises a KeyError because get_json_ref_counts and _garbage_collect_definitions try to look up those refs in the internal json_to_defs_refs mapping where they were never registered.

The fix checks membership in json_to_defs_refs before accessing it, so custom/external $ref values are skipped rather than causing a lookup failure. This applies to get_json_ref_counts, _garbage_collect_definitions, and get_schema_from_definitions.

Added a test covering the exact scenario from the issue: a type with __get_pydantic_json_schema__ returning a schema with local $ref/$defs.

title: fix: clear cached_property values in model_copy when update is provided
body:
Fixes #11955 (also reported as #11428 and #11542)

## The problem

When `model_copy(update={...})` is called, the new instance retains stale `cached_property` values from the original:

```python
m1 = MyModel(x=2)
m1.double  # caches 4

m2 = m1.model_copy(update={'x': 5})
m2.double  # returns 4 (wrong) -- should be 10
```

This happens because `cached_property` stores values in the instance `__dict__`, and `model_copy` copies `__dict__` wholesale without clearing these entries.

## The fix

After applying `update` in `model_copy`, clear all `cached_property` entries from the copied instance's `__dict__`. They will be lazily recomputed on next access with the correct field values.

When `update` is not provided, cached values are preserved since fields haven't changed.

## Tests

Added 5 test cases covering:
- Basic cached_property invalidation on update
- Cached values preserved without update (no regression)
- Deep copy with update
- Frozen model with update
- Multiple cached properties on same model

title: Support `exclude_if` in computed fields
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! -->
<!-- Unless your change is trivial, please create an issue to discuss the change before creating a PR -->

## Change Summary

This PR aims to support `serialization_exclude_if `in computed fields. This PR adds the ability to exclude the computed field both by passing a direct argument to the decorator, `exclude_if `(following the same naming convention we use for regular fields), and also if it receives an `Annotated `as in the example described in the linked issue.

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
from typing import Annotated

IntExcludeZero = Annotated[int, Field(exclude_if=lambda v: v == 0)]

# From annotated
class Model(BaseModel):
    @computed_field
    def a_computed_field(self) -> IntExcludeZero:
        return 0

obj = Model()
print(obj.model_dump())  # {}


# From decorator arg
class Model(BaseModel):
    @computed_field(exclude_if=exclude_if=lambda v: v == 0)
    def a_computed_field(self) -> int:
        return 0
obj = Model()
print(obj.model_dump())  # {}

# This is invalid, repeated exclude_if, raises PydanticUserError
class Model(BaseModel):
    @computed_field(exclude_if=exclude_if=lambda v: v == 0)
    def a_computed_field(self) -> IntExcludeZero:
        return 0

```



<!-- Please give a short summary of the changes. -->

title: Add `ascii_only` option to `StringConstraints`
body:
# feat: add ascii_only constraint to StringConstraints

## Change Summary

Implements the `ascii_only` option for `StringConstraints` as requested in #12300.

Previously, developers had to use an unintuitive regex pattern to enforce ASCII-only strings:

```python
username: Annotated[str, StringConstraints(pattern=r'^[\x00-\x7F]*$')]
```

This PR adds a clean boolean flag instead:

```python
username: Annotated[str, StringConstraints(ascii_only=True)]
```

Changes made:

- **pydantic-core**: Added `ascii_only` field to `StrConstrainedValidator`, implemented the check using Rust's native `.is_ascii()` before pattern matching for performance, and registered a new `StringNotAscii` error type
- **pydantic**: Exposed `ascii_only` parameter in `StringConstraints`, registered it in `_known_annotated_metadata.py`, and mapped it to the ASCII regex pattern in JSON Schema output
- **docs**: Added `string_not_ascii` section to `validation_errors.md`

## Related issue number

title: Standardize British English spelling to American English for consistency
body:
## Summary

Standardize scattered British English spellings to American English across source code, Rust comments, documentation, and tests for consistency with the rest of the codebase.

### Changes
- `behaviour` → `behavior` (comments, docstrings, variable names)
- `initialisation`/`initialise`/`initialised` → `initialization`/`initialize`/`initialized`
- `serialise` → `serialize`
- `customisation` → `customization`

### Scope
- **Python source** (`pydantic/`): 11 files
- **Rust comments** (`pydantic-core/src/`): 7 files
- **Documentation** (`docs/`): 6 files
- **Tests** (`tests/`, `pydantic-core/tests/`): 4 files

### Intentionally excluded
- `pydantic/v1/` — legacy compatibility shim, must not be modified
- `HISTORY.md` — auto-generated changelog entries from past contributors
- Error message strings — changing these would be a breaking change
- `tests/mypy/outputs/` — these match actual mypy output strings

## Why American English?

An analysis of the existing codebase shows that American English is overwhelmingly used as the standard:

| Word | American (US) | British (UK) | Ratio |
|------|--------------|--------------|-------|
| `serialization` vs `serialisation` | **969** occurrences | **0** | 100% US |
| `serialize`/`serializer` vs `serialise`/`serialiser` | **361** occurrences | **0** | 100% US |
| `behavior` vs `behaviour` (excl. v1/) | **83** in Python, **134** in Rust | **6** Python, **7** Rust | ~94% US |
| `initialization` vs `initialisation` | **11** occurrences | **1** | 92% US |
| `customize`/`customization` vs `customise`/`customisation` | **5** occurrences | **2** (only in v1/) | 100% US in v2 |

Additionally, **all public API identifiers** use American English exclusively:
- `extra_behavior` (config key, **324** occurrences)
- `ExtraBehavior` (Rust enum)
- `serialization_alias`, `serialize_as_any`, `model_serializer`

The British English instances fixed here are stray outliers in comments and docstrings — not a deliberate pattern.

## Test plan

- [x] `ruff check` passes on all modified Python files

- [x] No functional code changes — only comments, docstrings, variable names in comments, and doc anchors

title: Handle `PydanticOmit` in JSON schema definitions for duplicated union fields
body:
## Summary

Fixes #11553
Fixes #12706

When a type that raises `PydanticOmit` in `__get_pydantic_json_schema__` is referenced in multiple fields (e.g., in union types), pydantic-core moves it into a shared `definitions` section of the CoreSchema. The `definitions_schema()` method already catches `PydanticInvalidForJsonSchema` for definitions but did not catch `PydanticOmit`, causing it to propagate as an unhandled exception.

### Root Cause

`definitions_schema()` in `json_schema.py` catches `PydanticInvalidForJsonSchema` when processing definitions but had no handler for `PydanticOmit`. When a type raising `PydanticOmit` appeared in only one field, it worked fine (no definitions entry). But when the same type appeared in multiple fields, pydantic-core deduplicated it into a definition, and the unhandled `PydanticOmit` caused a crash.

### Fix

Follows the exact same pattern already established for `PydanticInvalidForJsonSchema`:

1. **Track omitted definitions** — New `_core_defs_omitted_for_json_schema: set[DefsRef]` stores definition refs that raised `PydanticOmit`
2. **Catch at definition time** — `definitions_schema()` now catches `PydanticOmit` and records the definition ref
3. **Re-raise at reference time** — `definition_ref_schema()` checks if the referenced definition was omitted and re-raises `PydanticOmit`, allowing the calling context (`union_schema`, `_named_required_fields_schema`, etc.) to handle it normally
4. **Propagate through helpers** — `get_schema_from_definitions()` and `_add_json_refs()` also check the omitted set for consistency
5. **Clear on populate** — If a definition is later successfully populated via `populate_defs()`, the omitted flag is cleared

## Test Plan

- [x] `test_pydantic_omit_in_definitions_with_duplicate_union_field` — Direct regression for #11553: custom type raising PydanticOmit in duplicate union fields
- [x] `test_pydantic_omit_in_definitions_single_field_still_works` — Single-field case (no definitions) still works
- [x] `test_pydantic_omit_with_type_alias_duplicate_fields` — Regression for #12706: MISSING sentinel with type aliases in duplicate fields
- [x] `test_pydantic_omit_conditional_in_definitions` — Mixed case: both omitted and kept types in unions
- [x] `test_skip_json_schema_with_base_model_in_duplicate_fields` — SkipJsonSchema with BaseModel type in duplicate fields (workaround from #11553 comments)
- [x] `test_pydantic_omit_with_type_statement_alias` — Python 3.12+ `type` keyword alias syntax (exact repro from #12706)
- [x] Full `test_json_schema.py` suite: 535 passed, 0 failures

title: Fix extra='allow' alias collision in serialization
body:
## Summary

Fixes #12884

When a model uses `extra='allow'` and a field has an alias, providing both the alias key and the field-name key in input causes serialization issues:
- `model_dump()` overwrites the declared field value with the extra value
- `model_dump_json()` emits duplicate keys

### Root Cause

In `GeneralFieldsSerializer.serialize_iterators()`, the extras iterator (`__pydantic_extra__`) processes entries without checking whether their keys collide with already-serialized field output keys.

### Fix

Track the output keys of fields that were actually serialized during the main dict iteration. When processing extras, skip any entry whose key matches an already-serialized field output key. This correctly handles:

- Field name vs alias collisions
- `serialization_alias` collisions with `by_alias=True`
- `by_alias=True` where alias differs from extra key (no false skips)
- Schema-excluded fields (their output keys are not tracked, so extras with the same name still appear)

### Changes

- **`pydantic-core/src/serializers/fields.rs`**: Added `AHashSet<String>` to collect serialized field output keys during main iteration, then skip colliding extras
- **`tests/test_serialize.py`**: Added 7 regression tests covering `model_dump`, `model_dump_json`, `by_alias`, `serialization_alias`, multiple fields, and excluded fields

## Test Plan

- [x] Existing `test_model_allow_extra` passes (previously failed with over-aggressive approach)
- [x] All 96 serialization tests pass
- [x] All 471 extra-related tests pass
- [x] All 838 alias-related tests pass
- [x] Lint checks pass (`ruff check` + `ruff format --check`)
- [x] Rust compiles cleanly with no warnings (`cargo check`)

title: Fix KeyError when custom JSON schema contains local $ref/$defs
body:
## Summary

Fixes #12145.

When `__get_pydantic_json_schema__` returns a schema that includes its own `$defs` and `$ref` entries, `TypeAdapter(...).json_schema()` crashes with `KeyError` because those refs aren't tracked in pydantic's internal `json_to_defs_refs` mapping.

Three methods in `GenerateJsonSchema` had the same pattern: catch `KeyError` on ref lookup, but only skip it for `http://`/`https://` URLs. Local refs from user-provided schemas hit the re-raise path.

The fix: treat all unresolvable `$ref` the same way -- skip them, since they aren't managed by pydantic regardless of whether they're remote URLs or local anchors from custom schema output.

## Test plan

- Added `test_custom_json_schema_with_local_defs_and_refs` covering both standalone `TypeAdapter` and model field usage
- All 529 existing `test_json_schema.py` tests pass

title: Fix KeyError on user-provided inline $defs with local $ref in JSON schema
body:
## Change Summary

When `__get_pydantic_json_schema__` returns a schema containing inline `$defs` and local `$ref` values (e.g. `#/$defs/Tire`), both `get_json_ref_counts()` and `_garbage_collect_definitions()` raise a `KeyError` because the local fragment reference is not registered in Pydantic's `json_to_defs_refs` mapping.

The existing code already skips external URL references (`http://`, `https://`). This extends that logic to also skip local JSON Pointer fragment references (those starting with `#`), which are self-contained within the user-provided schema and don't need resolution through Pydantic's definition system.

## Related issue number

fix #12145

title: fix(serialization): suppress spurious warnings for Union with exclude_unset=True
body:
Fixes #12888

## Problem
`model_dump(exclude_unset=True)` emits spurious `PydanticSerializationUnexpectedValue` warnings when a model contains `Union` fields. The serializer tries each Union member and warns when field counts do not match — even though the mismatch is caused by legitimately excluded unset fields, not a type error. Regression introduced in 2.13.0b2.

## Fix
In the Union serialization path, suppress warnings that are attributable to excluded-unset fields rather than genuine type mismatches.

## Testing
Added regression test reproducing the exact scenario from the issue.

## Change Summary

Fix an internal error in the pydantic mypy plugin when processing `BaseSettings` models with `SettingsConfigDict`. ## Change Summary
This PR adds `compare_as` callable in the `Field` class to add custom comparison. The classical example in the numpy ndarray, see #7307.  Note that `attrs` defines a similar `eq` callable (see the [docs](https://www.attrs.org/en/stable/comparison.html))

```python
import numpy

@define
class C:
   an_array = field(eq=attrs.cmp_using(eq=numpy.array_equal))

```
and the pydantic implementation looks like

```python
import numpy
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field


class C(BaseModel):
   an_array: np.ndarray = Field(compare_as=numpy.array_equal, default = np.array([1,2,3]))

   model_config = ConfigDict(allow_arbitrary_types = True)
```
Note that I intentionally added a `default = np.array([1,2,3])` to illustrate the example where `exclude_default = True` in the serialization, this callable can be forwarded to the Rust side. See this [discussion](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-core/pull/1114)

title: Ensure `__pydantic_private__` is set in `model_construct()` with user-defined `model_post_init()`
body:
Fixes #12813

## Problem

When a model defines a custom `model_post_init` but has no private attributes, `model_construct()` fails to set `__pydantic_private__`, causing `pickle.dumps()` to crash with `AttributeError`.

This happens because:
1. When there are no private attributes, the metaclass does not wrap `model_post_init` with `init_private_attributes`
2. `model_construct` only sets `__pydantic_private__` in the `elif` branch (when `__pydantic_post_init__` is falsy)
3. With a user-defined `model_post_init`, `__pydantic_post_init__` is truthy, so the `elif` branch is skipped
4. The user's `model_post_init` does not set `__pydantic_private__` → attribute never gets set

## Fix

After calling `model_post_init` in `model_construct`, check if `__pydantic_private__` was set. If not, set it to `None`.

## Test

Added `test_model_construct_pickle_with_model_post_init` that reproduces the exact scenario from the issue.

title: Bump actions/download-artifact from 6 to 8
body:
Bumps [actions/download-artifact](https://github.com/actions/download-artifact) from 6 to 8.
Release notes

Sourced from actions/download-artifact's releases.

v8.0.0

v8 - What's new

Direct downloads

To support direct uploads in actions/upload-artifact, the action will no longer attempt to unzip all downloaded files. Instead, the action checks the Content-Type header ahead of unzipping and skips non-zipped files. Callers wishing to download a zipped file as-is can also set the new skip-decompress parameter to false.

Enforced checks (breaking)

A previous release introduced digest checks on the download. If a download hash didn't match the expected hash from the server, the action would log a warning. Callers can now configure the behavior on mismatch with the digest-mismatch parameter. To be secure by default, we are now defaulting the behavior to error which will fail the workflow run.

ESM

To support new versions of the @actions/* packages, we've upgraded the package to ESM.

What's Changed

  • Don't attempt to un-zip non-zipped downloads by @​danwkennedy in actions/download-artifact#460
  • Add a setting to specify what to do on hash mismatch and default it to error by @​danwkennedy in actions/download-artifact#461

title: Fix AttributeError on repr of generic model with BaseModel bound
body:
## Summary

Fixes #12858

When a generic Pydantic model uses `BaseModel` as a type bound and is instantiated without parameterization, calling `repr()` or `print()` crashes with:

```
AttributeError: 'BaseModel' object has no attribute '__private_attributes__'
```

### Reproduction

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel
from typing import TypeVar, Generic

T = TypeVar('T', bound=BaseModel)

class Foo(BaseModel, Generic[T]):
    x: T

m = Foo(x={})  # succeeds
print(m)       # AttributeError
```

### Root Cause

When `T` is unparameterized, it resolves to `BaseModel` itself. `Foo(x={})` creates a raw `BaseModel()` instance as the field value. Raw `BaseModel` instances don't have `__private_attributes__`, `__pydantic_fields__`, or `__pydantic_computed_fields__` set — these are only added by the metaclass on proper subclasses.

The `__repr__` → `__repr_args__` → `__getattr__` chain then crashes when trying to access these missing attributes.

### Fix

1. **`__getattr__`**: Wrap the `__private_attributes__` lookup in try/except to gracefully handle raw BaseModel instances
2. **`__repr_args__`**: Use `getattr()` with empty dict fallbacks for `__pydantic_computed_fields__` and `__pydantic_fields__`, consistent with how `__pydantic_extra__` is already handled in the same method

### After fix

```python
m = Foo(x={})
print(m)       # Foo(x=BaseModel())
repr(m.x)      # 'BaseModel()'
```

title: fix: prevent computed field names from leaking into extra
body:
## Summary

- When a model has `extra='allow'` and computed fields, passing a value for a computed field name causes it to be stored in `__pydantic_extra__`, leading to duplicate keys in JSON output and incorrect `exclude_none` behavior.
- This fix strips computed field names from `__pydantic_extra__` after validation in both `__init__` and `model_construct`, so the computed property always takes precedence.

Fixes #12709

## Reproduction

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel, computed_field, ConfigDict

class BrokenModel(BaseModel):
    model_config = ConfigDict(extra='allow')
    name: str

    @computed_field
    def favorite_color(self) -> str:
        if self.name == 'John':
            return None
        return 'blue'

m = BrokenModel(name='John', favorite_color='red')

# Bug 1: duplicate keys in JSON
m.model_dump_json()
# '{"name":"John","favorite_color":"red","favorite_color":null}'

# Bug 2: exclude_none includes the extra value instead of computed
m.model_dump(exclude_none=True)
# {'name': 'John', 'favorite_color': 'red'}  ← should be {'name': 'John'}
```

## Changes

- **`pydantic/main.py`**: After `__init__` validation and in `model_construct`, pop any computed field names from `__pydantic_extra__` so they don't shadow the computed property.

title: Fix walrus operator precedence in `UrlConstraints.__get_pydantic_core_schema__()`
body:
## Summary

Fix incorrect walrus operator (`:=`) precedence in `UrlConstraints.__get_pydantic_core_schema__`.

## The Problem

In `pydantic/networks.py`, the current code is:

```python
if annotated_type := schema_to_mutate['type'] not in ('url', 'multi-host-url'):
```

Due to Python's operator precedence, the walrus operator `:=` has lower precedence than `not in`. This means the expression is evaluated as:

```python
annotated_type := (schema_to_mutate['type'] not in ('url', 'multi-host-url'))
```

So `annotated_type` is assigned a boolean (`True`), not the actual schema type string. The error message then reads:

```
'UrlConstraints' cannot annotate 'True'.
```

instead of the intended:

```
'UrlConstraints' cannot annotate 'string'.
```

## The Fix

Add parentheses to ensure the walrus operator captures the type string first:

```python
if (annotated_type := schema_to_mutate['type']) not in ('url', 'multi-host-url'):
```

Now `annotated_type` correctly holds the schema type (e.g. `'string'`, `'int'`), and the error message will display the actual type that was incorrectly annotated.
author: bysiber

title: Fix `__hash__` in `UuidVersion` and `PathType` to hash values instead of types
body:
## Summary

Fix `__hash__` methods in `UuidVersion` and `PathType` that always return the same hash value regardless of the instance's actual value.

## The Problem

Both `UuidVersion.__hash__` and `PathType.__hash__` use `hash(type(self.<attr>))` instead of `hash(self.<attr>)`:

```python
# UuidVersion
def __hash__(self) -> int:
    return hash(type(self.uuid_version))  # always hash(int) !

# PathType
def __hash__(self) -> int:
    return hash(type(self.path_type))     # always hash(str) !
```

Since `uuid_version` is always an `int` and `path_type` is always a `str`, `type()` always returns the same class, so all instances produce the same hash:

```python
>>> hash(type(1)) == hash(type(4)) == hash(type(7))
True
```

This means `UuidVersion(1)`, `UuidVersion(4)`, and `UuidVersion(7)` all hash identically, as do `PathType('file')`, `PathType('dir')`, and `PathType('socket')`. While equality checks still differentiate them, the hash collisions degrade performance wherever these objects are used as dict keys or in sets.

## The Fix

Hash the actual value instead of its type:

```python
# UuidVersion
def __hash__(self) -> int:
    return hash(self.uuid_version)

# PathType
def __hash__(self) -> int:
    return hash(self.path_type)
```

This is consistent with other metadata classes in the same file (e.g. `Strict.__hash__` returns `hash(self.strict)` and `AllowInfNan.__hash__` returns `hash(self.allow_inf_nan)`).

title: Allow any type form to be used in `validate_as()`
body:
## Change Summary

`validate_as()` currently rejects Pydantic's own `Annotated` type aliases like `NewPath`, `FilePath`, and `DirectoryPath` at the type-checking level. These are `_AnnotatedAlias` instances (e.g. `Annotated[Path, PathType('new')]`) rather than `type[T]`, so pyright flags them as invalid arguments.

I added an `Any` fallback overload that catches `Annotated` aliases and other type expressions not matched by `type[T]`. The overload resolution order is:

1. `type[_NewOutT]` — preserves precise type inference for concrete types
2. `EllipsisType` — handles the `...` case
3. `Any` — catches everything else (including `Annotated` aliases), returning `_Pipeline[_InT, Any]`

Once PEP 747 (`TypeForm`) lands in type checkers, this fallback can be replaced with a properly typed overload. I added a `TODO PEP 747` comment following the convention used elsewhere in the codebase.

fix #12845

title: Fix nested model schema deduplication in JSON schema generation
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! -->
<!-- Unless your change is trivial, please create an issue to discuss the change before creating a PR -->

## Change Summary

This fix addresses an issue where nested models with identical Input/Output schemas were not being properly deduplicated, resulting in duplicate schemas like 'User-Input' and 'User-Output' instead of a single 'User' schema.

The root cause was in the _DefinitionsRemapping.from_prioritized_choices() method, where the json_remapping dictionary was only mapping the original key to the remapped key, but not mapping intermediate simplified names.

For example, with alternatives:
  ['__main____Config-Input__1', '__main____Config-Input', 'Config-Input', 'Config']

When 'Config' was chosen as the canonical name, the mapping would only include: '__main____Config-Input__1' -> 'Config'

But after the first iteration, $refs would use 'Config-Input', and without a mapping from 'Config-Input' -> 'Config', subsequent iterations couldn't update those references.

The fix maps ALL alternatives from the remapped index onwards to ensure all intermediate simplification levels are covered.

Related FastAPI discussion: https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/discussions/14288


## Related issue number

Fix #12492

title: Preserve custom docstrings on stdlib dataclasses in JSON schema
body:
Fixes #12812

## Problem

`GenerateJsonSchema` suppresses all `__doc__` from stdlib dataclasses to avoid auto-generated signature docstrings (e.g. `"Foo(x: int = 1)"`) leaking as `description` in JSON schema. However, this also drops user-defined custom docstrings.

## Fix

Distinguish auto-generated docstrings from custom ones by checking if the docstring starts with `f"{cls.__name__}("` — the pattern Python uses for auto-generated dataclass docstrings.

Applied in both code paths:
- `_update_class_schema` (for BaseModel/class schemas)
- `dataclass_schema` (for stdlib dataclass schemas)

## Test

Added `test_stdlib_dataclass_custom_docstring_preserved` verifying:
- Custom docstrings on stdlib dataclasses are preserved as `description`
- Auto-generated docstrings are still suppressed

## Summary

- Add `exclude_if` callable parameter to `BaseModel.model_dump()`, `BaseModel.model_dump_json()`, `TypeAdapter.dump_python()`, and `TypeAdapter.dump_json()`
- The callable receives a field's serialized value and returns `True` to exclude that field

- For JSON methods, falls back to Python serialization + `json.dumps` when `exclude_if` is provided

## Example

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel

class MyModel(BaseModel):
    a: int
    b: str = ''
    c: list = []
    d: dict | None = None

m = MyModel(a=1, b='', c=[], d=None)

# Exclude empty/None values
m.model_dump(exclude_if=lambda v: not v and v is not False and v != 0)
# {'a': 1}

# Exclude only None
m.model_dump(exclude_if=lambda v: v is None)
# {'a': 1, 'b': '', 'c': []}
```

Fixes #10851

## Details

`AliasPath` currently only works with plain dictionaries for nested value extraction. When a model instance is passed as an intermediate value in the path, validation fails because pydantic-core uses item access (`__getitem__`) to traverse the path, and `BaseModel` does not support it.

### Changes:
1. **`BaseModel.__getitem__`**: Enables `model["field"]` by delegating to `getattr`, allowing pydantic-core's Rust validation to traverse model instances when resolving `AliasPath`.
2. **`AliasPath.search_dict_for_path` getattr fallback**: When `v[k]` fails and `k` is a string, falls back to `getattr(v, k)`, enabling `model_construct` to work with model instances in alias paths.

### Example (previously failing, now works):
```python
from pydantic import BaseModel, AliasPath, Field

class Nested(BaseModel):
    could_be_nested: int = 42

class Outer(BaseModel):
    regular_ol_val: int
    could_be_nested: int = Field(
        ..., validation_alias=AliasPath('nested', 'could_be_nested')
    )

Outer.model_validate({
    'regular_ol_val': 1,
    'nested': Nested(could_be_nested=2)
})
```

title: fix: prevent RecursionError in __eq__ with circular model references
body:
Fixes #10630

When a BaseModel instance has a self-referencing field (e.g., a.child = a), calling == triggers infinite recursion because __dict__ comparison recurses endlessly through the circular reference.

This adds a thread-local recursion guard that tracks (id(self), id(other)) pairs currently being compared. If the same pair is encountered again during a nested comparison, it returns True to break the cycle  matching Python's own behavior for recursive containers like lists and dicts.

The fix:
- Adds a module-level threading.local() guard
- Splits __eq__ into a guard wrapper + __eq_impl for the core logic
- Zero performance impact on non-circular comparisons (just one set lookup)
- Thread-safe via threading.local()

Tests added for:
- Self-referencing equality and inequality
- Same-object self-reference
- Mutual circular references (a -> b -> a)
- Deep circular chains (a -> b -> c -> a)
- Normal (non-circular) equality still works
- Non-BaseModel comparisons with circular refs

title: Fix discriminated union with PEP 695 TypeAliasType
body:
## Summary

Fixes #12771

When using PEP 695 `type` statement (`TypeAliasType`) to create a union alias for a discriminated union field, the discriminator was not applied correctly:

```python
type Pet = Cat | Dog

class Model(BaseModel):
    pet: Pet = Field(discriminator='pet_type')  # discriminator silently ignored
```

This caused **all** union members' validators to run for every input, instead of only the matching one based on the discriminator value.

**Root cause**: The `_apply_to_root` method in `_ApplyInferredDiscriminator` handles `nullable`, `definitions`, and `union` schema types when unwrapping the root schema to find the union to apply the discriminator to. However, `TypeAliasType` produces a `definition-ref` schema wrapping the union, which was not handled. The `definition-ref` fell through to the "not a union" fallback, which wrapped it in a single-member union. This resulted in all discriminator values mapping to the same `definition-ref` choice (the entire `Pet` union), so pydantic-core would try all union members for each discriminator value.

**Fix**: Added a `definition-ref` handler in `_apply_to_root` that resolves the reference and recursively applies the discriminator to the underlying schema (the union definition).

## Test plan

- [x] Added `test_discriminated_union_with_type_alias_type_pep695` - verifies correct type selection, error on invalid discriminator, and that the core schema uses `tagged-union`
- [x] Added `test_discriminated_union_with_nullable_type_alias_type_pep695` - verifies nullable variant works correctly
- [x] All 75 existing discriminated union tests pass (73 original + 2 new)

title: Fix pattern constraint dropped from JSON schema for Annotated types with validators
body:
## Summary

- Fixes a bug where combining an `Annotated` type with `BeforeValidator` (or other function validators) and an optional `Field` with a `pattern` constraint caused the `pattern` to be dropped from the generated JSON schema.
- The root cause was in `apply_known_metadata()`: for function wrapper schemas, constraints like `pattern` were always handled by creating a chain schema. Since JSON schema generation only examines the first step of a chain (the function wrapper with a bare `str` schema), the pattern was lost.
- The fix applies the constraint directly to the inner schema when it supports it, avoiding the unnecessary chain and preserving the constraint in the generated JSON schema.

title: Fix discriminated union with TypeAliasType (PEP 695)
body:
## Summary
- Fixed discriminated unions not working correctly with `TypeAliasType` (PEP 695 `type` keyword)
- Validators now only run for the discriminated union member, not all members

## Issue
When using the `type` keyword to create a type alias for a union (e.g., `type Pet = Cat | Dog`) and applying a discriminator via `Field(discriminator=...)`, the discriminator was not being properly applied. This caused all union member validators to run instead of just the correct one based on the discriminator value.

Fixes #12771

## Changes
- Modified `_apply_to_root` in `_discriminated_union.py` to handle `definition-ref` schemas
- When a definition-ref is encountered, the method now resolves the definition, applies the discriminator to the inner schema, updates the definition in place, and returns the unchanged definition-ref
- Added regression test `test_discriminated_union_with_type_alias_type`

## Test Plan
**Manual Testing:**
```python
from typing import Any, Literal
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, model_validator

class Cat(BaseModel):
    pet_type: Literal['cat']
    
    @model_validator(mode='before')
    @classmethod
    def validate_cat(cls, data: Any) -> Any:
        print(f"Validating Cat with {data}")
        return data

class Dog(BaseModel):
    pet_type: Literal['dog']
    
    @model_validator(mode='before')
    @classmethod
    def validate_dog(cls, data: Any) -> Any:
        print(f"Validating Dog with {data}")
        return data

type Pet = Cat | Dog

class Model(BaseModel):
    pet: Pet = Field(discriminator='pet_type')

# Before fix: Both validators run
# After fix: Only the correct validator runs
Model.model_validate({'pet': {'pet_type': 'cat'}})  # Now only calls Cat validator
Model.model_validate({'pet': {'pet_type': 'dog'}})  # Now only calls Dog validator
```

title: Ensure deterministic JSON schema defaults by sorting sets
body:
### Summary
Fixes #12754.

When a model field uses a `set` or `frozenset` as a default value, the generated JSON schema outputs the `default` list in a non-deterministic order due to Python's hash randomization. This causes issues for deterministic build systems (e.g., Bazel, Terraform) that expect identical outputs for identical inputs.

### The Fix
This PR adds a step in `GenerateJsonSchema.default_schema` to explicitly sort `set` and `frozenset` values before they are encoded into the JSON schema.

### Verification
I reproduced the issue locally using the script provided in #12754.
- **Before Fix:** The `default` field order changed randomly across multiple runs.
- **After Fix:** The `default` field is consistently sorted (alphabetically for strings/enums), ensuring deterministic output.

I verified that existing JSON schema tests pass (`pytest tests/test_json_schema.py`).

body:

Release notes

Sourced from urllib3's releases.

2.6.3

🚀 urllib3 is fundraising for HTTP/2 support

urllib3 is raising ~$40,000 USD to release HTTP/2 support and ensure long-term sustainable maintenance of the project after a sharp decline in financial support. If your company or organization uses Python and would benefit from HTTP/2 support in Requests, pip, cloud SDKs, and thousands of other projects please consider contributing financially to ensure HTTP/2 support is developed sustainably and maintained for the long-haul.

Thank you for your support.

Changes

  • Fixed a security issue where decompression-bomb safeguards of the streaming API were bypassed when HTTP redirects were followed. (CVE-2026-21441 reported by @​D47A, 8.9 High, GHSA-38jv-5279-wg99)
  • Started treating Retry-After times greater than 6 hours as 6 hours by default. (urllib3/urllib3#3743)
  • Fixed urllib3.connection.VerifiedHTTPSConnection on Emscripten. (urllib3/urllib3#3752)

2.6.2

🚀 urllib3 is fundraising for HTTP/2 support

urllib3 is raising ~$40,000 USD to release HTTP/2 support and ensure long-term sustainable maintenance of the project after a sharp decline in financial support. If your company or organization uses Python and would benefit from HTTP/2 support in Requests, pip, cloud SDKs, and thousands of other projects please consider contributing financially to ensure HTTP/2 support is developed sustainably and maintained for the long-haul.

Thank you for your support.

Changes

  • Fixed HTTPResponse.read_chunked() to properly handle leftover data in the decoder's buffer when reading compressed chunked responses. (urllib3/urllib3#3734)

2.6.1

🚀 urllib3 is fundraising for HTTP/2 support

urllib3 is raising ~$40,000 USD to release HTTP/2 support and ensure long-term sustainable maintenance of the project after a sharp decline in financial support. If your company or organization uses Python and would benefit from HTTP/2 support in Requests, pip, cloud SDKs, and thousands of other projects please consider contributing financially to ensure HTTP/2 support is developed sustainably and maintained for the long-haul.

Thank you for your support.

Changes

  • Restore previously removed HTTPResponse.getheaders() and HTTPResponse.getheader() methods. (#3731)

2.6.0

🚀 urllib3 is fundraising for HTTP/2 support

urllib3 is raising ~$40,000 USD to release HTTP/2 support and ensure long-term sustainable maintenance of the project after a sharp decline in financial support. If your company or organization uses Python and would benefit from HTTP/2 support in Requests, pip, cloud SDKs, and thousands of other projects please consider contributing financially to ensure HTTP/2 support is developed sustainably and maintained for the long-haul.

Thank you for your support.

Security

  • Fixed a security issue where streaming API could improperly handle highly compressed HTTP content ("decompression bombs") leading to excessive resource consumption even when a small amount of data was requested. Reading small chunks of compressed data is safer and much more efficient now. (CVE-2025-66471 reported by @​Cycloctane, 8.9 High, GHSA-2xpw-w6gg-jr37)
  • Fixed a security issue where an attacker could compose an HTTP response with virtually unlimited links in the Content-Encoding header, potentially leading to a denial of service (DoS) attack by exhausting system resources during decoding. The number of allowed chained encodings is now limited to 5. (CVE-2025-66418 reported by @​illia-v, 8.9 High, GHSA-gm62-xv2j-4w53)

[!IMPORTANT]

  • If urllib3 is not installed with the optional urllib3[brotli] extra, but your environment contains a Brotli/brotlicffi/brotlipy package anyway, make sure to upgrade it to at least Brotli 1.2.0 or brotlicffi 1.2.0.0 to benefit from the security fixes and avoid warnings. Prefer using urllib3[brotli] to install a compatible Brotli package automatically.

title: Improve ImportString error when internal imports fail
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! -->
<!-- Unless your change is trivial, please create an issue to discuss the change before creating a PR -->

## Change Summary

### What this PR does

Fixes https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/issues/12715.

Improves the error handling of `ImportString` so that internal import failures
(e.g. missing dependencies inside a module) are no longer masked as
`ImportError: No module named ...`.

If the missing module is not the requested import path (or its submodules),
the original `ModuleNotFoundError` is now correctly re-raised.

### Why

Previously, `ImportString` could incorrectly report that a module did not exist,
even when the real issue was a missing internal dependency. This made debugging
harder and hid the true cause of the failure.

### Changes

- Detect whether `ModuleNotFoundError.name` refers to the requested module
- Re-raise internal import errors instead of masking them
- Added tests covering the new behavior

title: Add experimental `MISSING` sentinel
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! -->
<!-- Unless your change is trivial, please create an issue to discuss the change before creating a PR -->

## Change Summary

Requires https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-core/pull/1711.

Fixes https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/issues/5326.
Fixes https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/issues/6928.
Fixes https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/issues/7712.
Fixes https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/issues/8394.
Fixes https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/issues/9057.
Fixes https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/issues/11705.
Fixes https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/issues/11843.

Example:

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel
from pydantic.experimental.missing_sentinel import MISSING


class A(BaseModel):
    a: int | MISSING = MISSING

a1 = A()
a1.model_dump()
#> {}

a2 = A(a=1)
a2.model_dump()
#> {'a': 1}

A.model_json_schema()
#> {'properties': {'a': {'title': 'A', 'type': 'integer'}}, 'title': 'A', 'type': 'object'}

class B(BaseModel):
    a: MISSING = MISSING


B.model_json_schema()
#> {'properties': {}, 'title': 'B', 'type': 'object'}
```

Things to consider:
- ~~Sentinel name: `UNSET` seems to be the best fit (and [matches `msgspec`](https://jcristharif.com/msgspec/api.html#msgspec.UNSET)), but will be confusing as we already have a concept of unset fields (tracked in `__pydantic_fields_set__`). These unset fields can already be excluded by specifying `exclude_unset=True` during serialization. If users explicitly set `exclude_unset=False` but the `UNSET` sentinel is still excluded, this will be confusing. One alternative could be `MISSING`: it also makes it a little bit clearer that the expected behavior is to have fields set to `MISSING` excluded from the output.~~ Went with `MISSING`.
- Sentinel location: currently defined in `pydantic-core`, but we need to expose it from the `experimental` module as we rely on the draft [PEP 661](https://peps.python.org/pep-0661/).
- ~~Should we create a new core schema for the `UNSET` sentinel? I'm currently using a `'literal'` schema, but not ideal for a couple reasons:~~
  - ~~The core validator uses equality to validate literal values, but sentinels should be compared using identity.~~
  - ~~If we happen to implement an optimization where we merge `'literal'` schemas together (e.g. `Literal[1] | UNSET` -> `Literal[1, UNSET]`), we would need to account for this in the JSON Schema generation logic).~~ Went with a new core schema type.

title: Fix Field constraint override in nested Annotated types
body:
Fixes #11361

## Problem

When using composed `Annotated` types with constraints and validators:

```python
String = Annotated[str, Field(max_length=10), AfterValidator(lambda v: v)]

class Model(BaseModel):
    name: Annotated[String, Field(max_length=20)]  # expected: 20, actual: 10
```

The override didn't work because both `MaxLen(10)` and `MaxLen(20)` ended up in metadata, and pydantic-core used the first one.

## Fix

Deduplicate constraint metadata by type in `FieldInfo._construct()`, keeping the last occurrence so overrides work correctly.

## Test

Added regression test in `tests/test_annotated.py`.

title: perf: optimize get_model_type_hints by reusing base class info
body:
### Description: The Forest Architecture (MRO Cut-off)
This PR introduces a significant architectural optimization to Pydantic's model field collection by implementing a "MRO Cut-off" mechanism. 

### The "Forest" Perspective:
Previously, every time a Pydantic model was defined, the system performed a full MRO traversal to re-evaluate type hints. This was like re-exploring the entire forest for every new tree planted. In large systems with deep inheritance, this leads to quadratic overhead.

### Strategic Improvements:
- **MRO Cut-off**: We now introduce `__pydantic_type_hints__` as a cached "Map of the Forest" on each model.
- **Incremental Inheritance**: When defining a subclass, the system stops traversing the MRO as soon as it encounters a base class with already resolved hints. It simply merges the parent's "Map" with its own "Direct Annotations".
- **Decoupling from `typing` overhead**: By cutting off redundant ancestral processing, we drastically reduce the number of expensive calls to `try_eval_type` and namespace resolution logic.

### Why this addresses previous regressions:
The previous approach of copying `FieldInfo` objects created hidden overhead in complex recursive models. This new architecture focuses purely on the **Information Flow** (Type Hints), ensuring that once a type is resolved in the hierarchy, it never needs to be re-processed by any descendant.

### Impact:
For models with inheritance depth $D$ and total fields $N$, the complexity is reduced from $O(D \times N)$ to effectively $O(1)$ lookup for inherited fields + $O(Direct\_Fields)$ for new ones. This provides true linear scalability for large-scale generated schemas.

---
**Verified with:**
- [x] Multiple Inheritance Merging Tests
- [x] Recursive Structure Safety Tests
- [x] Cache Immutability & Integrity Tests
- [x] All logic confirmed via pure-logic mock verification.

title: Do not re-use prebuilt serializers/validators on rebuilds
body:
## Change Summary

- Adds a `_use_prebuilt` keyword argument to `SchemaValidator` and `SchemaSerializer` (from pydantic-core: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-core/pull/1895)
- Defaults to `True` so existing behavior is preserved (prebuilt optimization is used)
- Only disables prebuilt when `_use_prebuilt=False` which happens only during `model_rebuild(force=True)`
- Threads the flag through pydantic's `create_schema_validator` ⇒ `complete_model_class` ⇒ `model_rebuild`

The existing prebuilt tests should pass because normal schema creation uses `_use_prebuilt=True` by default, but the GC bug in #12446 is fixed (confirmed in local testing with both PRs) because `model_rebuild(force=True)` passes `_use_prebuilt=False`.

## Related issue number

- Closes #12446.
- ~~Requires upstream work in pydantic-core~~ **merged** with PR at https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-core/pull/1895

## Checklist

* [ ] The pull request title is a good summary of the changes - it will be used in the changelog
* [ ] Unit tests for the changes exist
* [ ] Tests pass on CI
* [ ] Documentation reflects the changes where applicable
* [ ] My PR is ready to review, **please add a comment including the phrase "please review" to assign reviewers**


---

Further details from old PR:

### Change Summary

This PR adds a `_use_prebuilt: bool = True` parameter to `SchemaValidator.__init__` and `SchemaSerializer.__init__` to fix the memory leak described in #1894.

### Problem

PR #1616 introduced `PrebuiltValidator`/`PrebuiltSerializer` as a memory optimization that reuses existing validators/serializers from model classes. However, when `model_rebuild(force=True)` is called on recursive models:

1. `Collection.model_rebuild()` creates a new validator
2. When building, it encounters `BlockGroup` and `PredictiveModel` in a union
3. Since those models have `__pydantic_complete__=True`, their existing validators are wrapped in `PrebuiltValidator` (a strong `Py<SchemaValidator>` reference)
4. Later, when `BlockGroup` and `PredictiveModel` are rebuilt, they get NEW validators
5. But `Collection`'s validator still holds references to the OLD validators via `PrebuiltValidator`
6. The old validators can never be garbage collected

This causes unbounded RSS growth (~50MB per 1000 rebuild cycles).

### Solution

- Add `_use_prebuilt: bool = True` parameter to `SchemaValidator::py_new` and `SchemaSerializer::py_new`
- When `_use_prebuilt=False`, set `use_prebuilt=false` in `DefinitionsBuilder`, which skips the prebuilt optimization
- Thread `use_prebuilt` through `DefinitionsBuilder` so nested builds respect the same setting
- Pass `_use_prebuilt=False` from `__reduce__` to maintain correct unpickling behavior (avoiding prebuilt during reconstruction)

### Unchanged

- Normal model creation still uses the prebuilt optimization (`_use_prebuilt=True` by default)
- Existing behavior is preserved for all non-rebuild scenarios

## Related Issues

- Fixes https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-core/issues/1894 (RSS growth on model rebuild)
- Should also resolve https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic-core/issues/1893 (stale referents on rebuild)
- Also (incidentally) solves https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/issues/12696

title: Add regression test for pickling objects with `@validate_call`
body:
## Summary

This PR adds a regression test to ensure that objects with methods decorated with \@validate_call\ can be properly pickled when the classes are defined at module level.

## Issue Reference

Closes #7846

## Details

The issue reported that pickling a \UserDict\ subclass with a \@validate_call\ decorated \__setitem__\ method would fail with:
\\\
AttributeError: Can't pickle local object 'GenerateSchema._common_field_schema.<locals>.json_schema_update_func'
\\\

Based on the comments in #7846, this issue appears to have been fixed in a previous pydantic-core update. This PR adds a regression test to ensure the fix remains in place.

## Test

The test creates:
- A simple \BaseModel\ subclass (\_PickleTestModel\)
- A \UserDict\ subclass with \@validate_call\ on \__setitem__\ (\_PickleTestDict\)

It then verifies that instances can be pickled and unpickled without errors.

## Notes

The test classes must be defined at module level to be importable/picklable - this matches the real-world use case described in the original issue.

title: Support Root models with `Literal` root types as discriminator field types

## Summary

- This is useful when using code generators like `datamodel-code-generator` that wrap Literal types in RootModel classes

When using a `RootModel[Literal['X']]` as a field type for a discriminator, Pydantic previously failed with:

pydantic.errors.PydanticUserError: Model 'OperationActionData' needs field 'action' to be of type `Literal`

Added handling in `_infer_discriminator_values_for_inner_schema` for `'model'` schema type with `'root_model': True` flag. This unwraps the RootModel to get the inner Literal schema.

title: Handle whitespace-only strings in min_length validation
body:
### Summary
This PR ensures that string fields with a positive `min_length` constraint
do not accept values consisting only of whitespace characters.

### Motivation
Whitespace-only strings technically satisfy character length checks but are
semantically empty and commonly invalid in real-world data models.

### Changes
- Update `constr_length_validator` to validate length using stripped values
  without mutating the original input.
- Add tests covering whitespace-only and valid non-whitespace strings.

### Compatibility
- Existing behavior remains unchanged when `min_length` is not specified.
- No transformation of input values is performed.

Based on tag `v1.10.13`.

title: Fix RecursionError in BaseModel equality with circular references
body:
## Summary

Fix `RecursionError` when comparing `BaseModel` instances that contain circular self-references.

## Changes

- Added `try-except RecursionError` handlers in `BaseModel.__eq__` to gracefully handle circular references
- When `RecursionError` is caught during comparison, we return `True` (assuming equal structure)
- Added tests for self-referential and mutual-reference equality scenarios

## Why This Approach

This implementation has **zero performance overhead** for normal (non-circular) comparisons:
- No additional tracking variables or ContextVar usage
- No set allocations or lookups on every comparison
- The try-except only triggers when `RecursionError` actually occurs

This addresses the performance concerns raised in PR #11581 which proposed using `ContextVar` tracking for every equality comparison.

## Behavior

| Scenario | Result |
|----------|--------|
| Same structure circular refs | `True` |
| Different types | `False` (detected before recursion) |
| Different values in non-circular fields | `False` (detected before recursion) |
| Same instance (`a == a`) | `True` |

## Example

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel
from typing import Optional

class SelfRef(BaseModel):
    value: int = 0
    ref: Optional['SelfRef'] = None

a = SelfRef()
a.ref = a  # a refers to itself

a2 = SelfRef()
a2.ref = a2  # a2 refers to itself

# Before: RecursionError
# After: True (same structure)
a == a2
```

## Testing

- Added `test_self_referential_equality` for direct self-reference scenarios
- Added `test_mutual_reference_equality` for mutual circular references
- All existing equality tests continue to pass

Fixes #10630

title: fix(equality): prevent RecursionError in __eq__ with self-referential models
body:
## Summary

This PR fixes #10630 by adding cycle detection to `BaseModel.__eq__` to prevent `RecursionError` when comparing models with circular references.

### Problem

When comparing two self-referential models, the `__dict__` comparison recursively calls `__eq__` on nested BaseModel instances, leading to infinite recursion:

```python
from pydantic import BaseModel

class A(BaseModel):
    a: 'A' = None

a = A()
a.a = a  # self-reference

a2 = A()
a2.a = a2

a == a2  # RecursionError!
```

### Solution

- Added thread-local storage (`_eq_context`) to track pairs of objects currently being compared
- Track `(id(self), id(other))` pairs during comparison
- Return `True` when a cycle is detected (structural equality up to that point)
- Clean up the visited set after comparison completes

This approach:
- Is **thread-safe** via `threading.local()`
- Has **minimal overhead** for non-recursive comparisons (only `hasattr()` check)
- Handles self-references, mutual references, and cyclic graphs correctly

### Changes

- `pydantic/main.py`: Added `threading` import, `_eq_context` thread-local, and cycle detection logic in `__eq__`
- `tests/test_main.py`: Added `test_equality_self_referential`, `test_equality_mutual_references`, `test_equality_cyclic_graph`

## Test plan

- [x] Self-reference self-equality: `a == a` where `a.a = a` returns `True`
- [x] Two self-referential objects: `a1 == a2` where both have self-references returns `True`
- [x] Different structures: Self-reference vs non-self-reference returns `False`
- [x] Mutual references: `a -> b -> a` compared to `c -> d -> c` returns `True`
- [x] Cyclic graphs: `n1 -> n2 -> n3 -> n1` compared to identical structure returns `True`
- [x] Existing equality tests still pass

---
Ahmed Adel Bakr Alderai

title: fix: prevent RecursionError in BaseModel.__eq__ for self-referencing models
body:
Fixes #10630

## Description
This PR prevents `RecursionError` when comparing Pydantic models with self-references (cycles), addressing issue #10630.

## Implementation
- Introduced a `_recursion_ignore` thread-local set in `pydantic/main.py`.
- Modified `BaseModel.__eq__` to track pairs of `(id(self), id(other))` currently being compared.
- If a cycle is detected (pair already exists in set), `__eq__` returns `True` (assuming equality for the cycle), aligning with Python's standard recursive equality behavior.

## Verification
- Added regression test `tests/test_issue_10630.py` which reproduces the crash and verifies the fix.
- Ran core tests (`pytest tests/test_main.py`) to ensure no regressions.

title: test: add regression test for recursion error in self-referencing models (Issue #10630)
body:
### Description
This PR adds a regression test for Issue #10630, verifying that comparing distinct self-referencing `BaseModel` instances (`m1 == m2`) does not trigger a `RecursionError`.

While the cycle detection logic in `BaseModel.__eq__` currently handles this case correctly, there was no explicit test coverage for this potentially fragile behavior. This test ensures that future optimizations to `__eq__` do not inadvertently regress this fix.

### Changes
- Added `tests/test_issue_10630.py`:
  - Defines a recursive `Model` class.
  - Creates two distinct instances with self-references (`m1.x = m1`, `m2.x = m2`).
  - Asserts `m1 == m2` passes without stack overflow.
